articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: याडियाका तीन नयाँ स्मार्ट विद्युतीय स्कुटर नेपाली बजारमा, १० हजार छुटको अफर
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालका लागि याडिया (YADEA) को आधिकारिक वितरक कुजु नेपाल प्रा. लि. ले नयाँ पुस्ताका GS70, GT70 र GTM90 विद्युतीय स्कुटरहरू नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। आधुनिक प्रविधि, उत्कृष्ट कार्यक्षमता र नेपाली सडक अनुकूल डिजाइन गरिएका यी स्कुटरहरूले दैनिक सहरी यात्रादेखि लामो दूरीको यात्रासम्मका फरक-फरक आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

सार्वजनिक गरिएका तीन मोडेलमध्ये GS70 लाई दैनिक सहरी यात्राका लागि किफायती विकल्पका रूपमा तयार पारिएको छ। यसमा २.१ kWh LFP ब्याट्री र २.८ kW पिक मोटर दिइएको छ, जसले एकपटकको पूर्ण चार्जमा १०५ किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज प्रदान गर्छ। लामो दूरीको यात्रा गर्नेहरूका लागि GT70 उपयुक्त छ, जसमा ५.७ kWh को डुअल LFP ब्याट्री (३.६ kWh फिक्स्ड र २.१ kWh रिमुभेबल) तथा ३.७ kW पिक मोटर रहेको छ। यसले २२० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ भने रिमुभेबल ब्याट्रीका कारण घर वा कार्यालयमा सहजै चार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ। प्रिमियम श्रेणीको GTM90 मा ३.६ kWh लिथियम ब्याट्री र ५ kW पिक मोटर जडान गरिएको छ, जसले ८० किमि प्रतिघण्टाको उच्च गति र १५० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ।

प्रविधि र सुरक्षाका हिसाबले यी नयाँ स्कुटरहरू निकै आधुनिक छन्। ती सबैमा TFT स्मार्ट डिस्प्ले, ब्लुटुथ कनेक्टिभिटी, मोबाइल नेभिगेसन मिररिङ, याडिया स्मार्ट एप, कि-लेस प्रणाली र ५ जनासम्म प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने 'फ्यामिली सेयरिङ' सुविधा उपलब्ध छ। यात्रालाई थप सुरक्षित र सहज बनाउन ट्र्याक्सन कन्ट्रोल सिस्टम (TCS), क्रुज कन्ट्रोल, हिल होल्ड, हिल डिसेन्ट कन्ट्रोल र डुअल डिस्क ब्रेकजस्ता अत्याधुनिक प्रविधि समावेश गरिएका छन्।

कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलका ब्याट्रीमा ३ वर्ष वा ५०,००० किलोमिटरसम्मको दीर्घकालीन वारेन्टी प्रदान गरेको छ। हाल यी स्कुटरहरू देशभर रहेका २० वटा आधिकारिक याडिया डिलरशिपहरू मार्फत उपलब्ध छन्। साथै, सार्वजनिक गरिएको अवसरमा नाइमा अटो शो (NAIMA Auto Show) सम्म लागू हुने गरी कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलमा रु. १०,००० को विशेष नगद छुट दिएको छ। ग्राहकहरूले नजिकैको शोरुममा गई टेस्ट राइड तथा फाइनान्सिङ सुविधाबारे थप जानकारी लिन सक्नेछन्।

articles.title: खल्तीबाट डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा दैनिक १ लाख र बम्परमा १० लाख जित्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । आईएमई खल्ती लिमिटेडले अर्थ मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गतको आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागद्वारा सञ्चालित ‘करदाता प्रोत्साहन उपहार कार्यक्रम, २०८३’ मा आफ्ना प्रयोगकर्तालाई सहभागी गराउने भएको छ। खल्तीमार्फत रु १०० भन्दा बढीको योग्य डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा ग्राहकहरू स्वतः दैनिक तथा पाक्षिक उपहार छनोटमा सहभागी हुनेछन्।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत दैनिक एक जना विजेताले कर कट्टीपछि रु. १ लाख र प्रत्येक १५ दिनमा एक जना बम्पर विजेताले रु १० लाख प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। भुक्तानीको विवरण सुरक्षित रूपमा राजस्व विभागको प्रणालीमा पुग्ने र उपहार कुपन स्वतः सिर्जना भई खल्ती एपमै देखिने व्यवस्था मिलाइएको छ। विभागले प्रत्येक महिनाको १ र १६ गते स्वचालित प्रणालीबाट विजेता छनोट गरी एसएमएस, इमेल तथा खल्तीमार्फत जानकारी गराउनेछ।

बिलमा आधारित कारोबार प्रवर्द्धन गरी डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र र राष्ट्रिय राजस्व प्रणालीलाई सुदृढ बनाउने लक्ष्यका साथ यो सहकार्य गरिएको आईएमई खल्तीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रेग्मीले बताएका छन्।

articles.title: सर्वसाधारणको रकम गरिमा विकास बैंकले झ्वाम पार्दै, झ्वाम पार्ने को–को ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । के तपाईंको गरिमा विकास बैंकमा खाता छ ?के तपाईंले आफुले मेहेनत गरेको रकम गरिमा बिकास बैंकमा राख्नु भएको छ ? यदी छ भने तपाईंका लागि आज दुखको खबर छ । कारण हो, ग्राहकले राखेको रकम बैंकको भवन किन्दा अपचलन गरेर प्रचलित मूल्यभन्दा बढी मूल्यामा किनिएको छ । प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन र प्रचलित बजार मूल्यलाई समेत लत्याउँदै बैंक व्यवस्थापनले ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरेको छ । सर्वसाधारणले दुःख गरेर बैंकमा जम्मा गरेको निक्षेप सुरक्षित छ त?भन्ने प्रश्न पनि उठिरहेको छ ।

गरिमा विकास बैंकले काठमाडौँको बालुवाटारमा ३७ आनाभन्दा बढी जग्गा र त्यसमा बनेको घर खरिद गर्दा प्रचलित बजार मूल्य र स्वयं प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनलाई समेत लत्याउँदै करिब ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरिएको भेटिएको छ। बजार मन्दीमा रहेका बेला प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन भन्दा दोब्बर मूल्य हालेर जग्गा र भवन किनिएको छ ।

काठमाडौंको बालुवाटारमा कित्ता नम्बर ४९ मा रहेको २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसा अर्थात् ३७ दशमलव २६ आना जग्गा र ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिटको बनेको यो आरसीसी भवन शिखर इन्स्योरेन्सका पूर्वअध्यक्ष राजेन्द्रप्रसाद श्रेष्ठको २०८२ सालमा गरिमा विकास बैंकले केन्द्रीय कार्यालय बनाउन खरिद ग¥यो ।

बैंकले यो जग्गा खरिद गर्दा प्रतिआना १ करोड ५६ लाख १४ हजार ९२२ रुपैयाँ तिरेको देखिन्छ । अर्थात २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसाको जग्गाको मूल्या ५८ करोड १८ लाख १२ हजार रुपैयाँ बैकलाई पर्न गयो। अब यही जग्गामा रहेको यो भवनको क्षेत्रफल ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट रहेको छ ।

बैंकले यो भवनको मूल्य ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरेको देखिन्छ । वर्गफिटमा हिसाब गर्दा पनि प्रति वर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरको छ । तपाईलाई यो खरिद मूल्य सायद सामान्य नै लाग्यो होला? यो सामान्य घरजग्गा किनबेच देखिए तापनि, प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बैंकको हालेको रकम जुधाउँदा भने ठूलो अन्तर देखिन्छ ।

प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बजार मूल्यको वास्तविकता

पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले बैंक धितोकै लागि तयार पारेको प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन अनुसार सो क्षेत्रमा जग्गाको स्थानीय बजार दर प्रतिआना ८० लाख रुपैयाँ मात्र छ। स्थानीय व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार पनि बजारको अधिकतम मूल्य ९० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी पर्दैन।

प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनमा सडकको अधिकार क्षेत्र कट्टा गरी कायम भएको १ रोपनी १३ आना ३ पैसा जग्गाको कुल बजार मूल्य १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार मात्रै कायम गरेको छ । पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कमर्सियल भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको २३ करोड ८३ लाख ९९ हजार यो जग्गाको मूल्या कायम गरेको छ । फेयर मार्केट भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार कायम गर्यो ।

डिस्ट्रेस भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भने १४ करोड १६ लाख ७८ हजार कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कायम गरेको छ । तर बंैकले बैंकले भने सोही जग्गालाई ५८ करोड १८ लाखभन्दा बढी भुक्तानी गर्यो। यो खेल जग्गामा मात्र रोकिएन, भवन खरिदमा पनि उस्तै अस्वाभाविक मूल्या हालियो ।

४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट क्षेत्रफल रहेको सो भवनको मूल्य बैंकले ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँ तय गरेर खरिद ग¥यो। अर्थात् प्रतिवर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँ! निर्माण व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार काठमाडौँमा अत्यन्त लक्जरियस सामग्री प्रयोग गर्दा पनि नयाँ भवन निर्माण खर्च प्रतिवर्गफिट अधिकतम ४ हजारदेखि ६ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म मात्र पुग्छ। प्रतिवर्गफिट ६ हजार नै मान्ने हो भने पनि २८ करोड ५७ लाख पर्ने भवनलाई बैंकले १० करोड ७४ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी अतिरिक्त मूल्य हालेर किनेको देखिन्छ ।

जग्गामा २४ करोड ६५ लाख र घरमा १० करोड ७४ लाख गरी कुल ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी रकम बजार मूल्य र प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कनभन्दा बढी मूल्य हालिएको छ । घर–जग्गा बजारमा मन्दी छाएका बेला प्रचलित भाउभन्दा निकै माथि गएर गरिएको यो निर्णयमा गरिमा विकास बैंकका सञ्चालक अनिल रेग्मी, ईश्वरीप्रसाद ढकाल र सीईओ माधवप्रसाद उपाध्याय लगायतको भूमिका देखिन्छ ।

सर्वसाधारण निक्षेपकर्ताको पसिनाको कमाईमाथि बैंकका सञ्चालक र उच्च व्यवस्थापनबाट भएको यो अस्वाभाविक खर्चले बैंकको संस्थागत सुशासन र नियमनकारी निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकको अनुगमनमाथि ठूलो प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ।

articles.title: फोनिज काठमाडौँको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा पदयात्रा सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा फोनिज पदयात्रा सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसर पारेर आज शनिवार काठमाडौँको साँखु–बज्रयोगिनी हुँदै मणिचूड दहसम्म पदयात्रा तथा विभिन्न गुम्बा तथा मन्दिर परिसरमा वृक्षरोपण गरेका हुन् । काठमाडौँ जिल्ला अन्तरगत फोनिज आवद्ध प्रतिनिधिहरू, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि र विभिन्न जातिय संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागितामा साँखुमा भेला भइ बज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर परिसरबाट करिव १७ किलोमिटिरको दूरीमा पदयात्रा गरेका थिए ।

पदयात्रापछि मणिचूड दहमा भएको औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वक्ताहरूले धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धन र संरक्षणमा आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहेको बताएका छन् । कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै शंकरापुर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का अध्यक्ष पोते थिङले मणिचूड दहको महत्वबारे प्रकाश पार्दै प्रचारप्रसारको अभाव तथा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज वन क्षेत्रको निश्चित मापदण्डका कारण अझै ओझेलमा परेको बताए । मणिचूड दह र त्यस क्षेत्रमा रहेका हरेक धार्मिक तथा साँस्कृतिक सम्पदाको संरक्षण र प्रवद्र्धनका साथै थप व्यवस्थापन गर्न वनसंग जोडिएको कानुनलाई परिमार्जण गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखे ।

त्यस्तै शिवपुरी नागार्जुन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष श्यामकुमार वाइबाले निकुञ्जभित्र रहेको मणिचूड दह बौद्ध र हिन्दू दुवै धर्मालम्बीहरू पवित्र तिर्थस्थलको रूपमा मान्दै आएको बताए । विशेष गरि जनजातिजातिको बहुल्यता रहेको त्यस क्षेत्रमा बौद्ध धर्मालम्बीहरूले विभिन्न समयमा पूजापाठ, मोन्लाम लगायत साउन महिने जलयात्रा, जनैपूर्णिमा लगायत साँस्कृतिक पर्वहरू मनाउने भएकोले थप महत्व रहेको बताए । अहिले निकुञ्ज, स्थानीय तह र मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिबीचको समन्वयमा व्यवस्थित बनाउने रणनीति रहेको बताए ।

कार्यक्रममा राष्ट्रि शहिद तथा शान्ति स्मारक पार्क र गोकर्ण यज्ञडोल सामुदायिक वन उपभोक्त समितिका अध्यक्ष सुर्दशन सिग्देलले वन, जंगल, जल र जमिनको संरक्षणमा जनजाति समुदायको उल्लेख्य भूमिका रहेको बताउँदै आफ्नो साँस्कृतिक पहिचान र अधिकारसँग जाडिएको क्षेत्रमा राज्यले दुःख दिन नहुने बताए । जनजाति समुदायले विशेष गरि प्रकृतिको पुजा गर्ने चाडपर्वलाई साँस्कृतिक पहिचानको रूपमा विश्वमाझ चिनाउन सफल रहेको बताउँदै राष्ट्रिय शहिद पार्क वन क्षेत्रमा समेत विभन्नि जातजातिको अस्तित्व समेट्ने गरि भिलेजग्रामको निर्माण गरिएको बताए ।

फोनिज बागमति प्रदेश समितिका महासचिव राजु नापितले फोनिजले पत्रकारितालाई आफ्नो पेसागत हकअधिकारमात्र नभएर भाषा, कला, संस्कृतिको संरक्षण र सम्वद्र्धनमा विशेष योगदान पु¥याउँदै आइरहेको बताए । फोनिज बागमति प्रदेशभित्र पत्रकारहरूलाई एकीकृत गराउँदै समुदायको पहिचान र अधिकार सुनिश्चित गराउन समेत जिल्लासमितिहरूले सक्रियतापूर्वक गतिविधि सञ्चालन गराउँदै आएको बताए ।

त्यस्तै फोनिज संघीय समितिका सचिव सुनिल महर्जनले फोनिज पदयात्राले रमाइलो मात्र नभइ अनुसन्धानका आयाम बुझ्न पाएको बताए । मणिचूडको सुन्दर ऐतिहासिक धार्मिक पर्यटकीय स्थल प्रकृतिप्रेमी र आध्यात्मिक शान्ति चाहनेहरूका लागि विशेष रहने बताउँदै पत्रकारिताको माध्यमबाट प्रचारप्रसारलाई तिब्रता दिनुपर्ने बताए । फोनिजले नेपालभित्र रहेका आदिवासी जनजाति समुदायसंग जोडिएका कला, भाषा, धर्म संस्कृति र पहिचान बोकेका विषयवस्तुहरूको अध्ययन र अनुसन्धान गरि विश्वसामु चिनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेको बताए ।

नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला समितिका अध्यक्ष भिमबहादुर लामाले सामाजिक एकता र सद्भाव कायम उद्देश्यका साथ फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसलाई सार्थक पार्न पदयात्रा तथा वृक्षरोपण कार्यक्रमको आयोजना गरिएको बताए । उनले जनजाति पत्रकारहरूको पेसागत क्षमतालाई दरिलो बनाउन अध्ययन, अनुसन्धान र आलेख लेखनमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले धार्मिक पर्यटकीय क्षेत्र तथा जनजाति समुदायको साँस्कृतिक तथा धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको क्षेत्र साँखु, बज्रयोगिनी र मणिचूड दहको यात्रा तय गरेको बताए । राज्य र पहुँचवाला समूहहरूबाट आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको थातथालोमा जलविद्युत गुरूयोजनाहरू सञ्चालन गर्ने, विकास निर्माण र राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको नाममा परिवारहरू विस्थापित बनाएको अध्यक्ष लामाले आरोप लगाए ।

फोनिज काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिका सचिव रत्नमान महर्जनले सञ्चालन गरेको कार्यक्रममा नेपाल प्रहरीका पूर्व डिआइजी देउती गुरूङ, गोकर्णेश्वर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का वडा सदस्य सुमन लामा, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ काठमाडौँ शाखा उपाध्यक्षद्वाय कमल राना मगर, कान्ति न्यौपाने, सहसचिब बिक्रम रत्न, मणिचूड मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष भिम घ्लान, नेपाल बौद्ध धर्म संरक्षण संघका महासचिव उमा गुरूङ, साँस्कृतिक युवा समूहका अध्यक्ष वेचन लामा, समाजसेवी किरण मोक्तान, सोफिया पाख्रिन लगायत अतिथि रहेका थिए । पदयात्रामा फोनिजकर्मी तथा विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधि गरि ६८ जनाको सहभागीता रहेको थियो ।

articles.title: हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्षको बहारः ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बाग्मती प्रदेशको राजधानी हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ लाई लक्षित गर्दै ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइन लागिएको पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अन्तर्गत सरसफाइ थालिएको हो ।

यो वर्ष बाग्मतीको प्रादेशिक राजधानीस्थित हेटौँडा उपमहानगरपालिकाले पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मनाउँदैछ । पर्यटन वर्षको कार्यक्रम अन्तर्गत सून्य फोहोर अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । यहि अभियान अन्तर्गत शनिवार हातमा कुचो र बोरा बोकेर जनप्रतिनिधि, सुरक्षाकर्मी, टोल विकास संस्थाका पदाधिकारी र स्थानीयवासी सडकमा निस्किए । हेटौँडाका सडकदेखि टोलसम्म सरसफाइ गर्दै उनीहरूले ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियान शुरु गरेका हुन् ।

फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई केवल सरसफाइ अभियानका रूपमा नभई पर्यटन, वातावरण संरक्षण र नागरिक संस्कृतिसँग जोडिएको दीर्घकालीन अभियानका रूपमा अघि बढाइने योजना उपमहानगरपालिकाको छ । उपमहानगरपालिकाले ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइने पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अघि सारिएको हो ।

मुख्य तथा सहायक सडक, सार्वजनिक स्थल र पर्यटकीय क्षेत्रको सरसफाइसँगै वृक्षारोपण र सौन्दर्यीकरणलाई पनि अभियानको प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ । टोल विकास संस्था नगर समन्वय समितिको संयोजनमा सुरु भएको अभियान नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोल विकास संस्थामा सुरु गरिएको छ । पर्यटन वर्षको अवसरमा सुरु गरिएको ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियानले नगरको स्वच्छता र सौन्दर्य कायम राख्दै हेटौँडालाई पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यका रूपमा चिनाउन सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको दाबी छ ।

पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मा हेटौँडामा आन्तरिक तथा बाह्य पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउने उपमहानगरपालिकाको लक्ष्य छ । पर्यटकलाई आकर्षित गर्न नयाँ गन्तव्यको प्रचारसँगै शहरको स्वच्छता, सौन्दर्य र व्यवस्थित वातावरणलाई पनि प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ ।

यही उद्देश्यले सुरु गरिएको यो अभियानलाई नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोलसम्म विस्तार गरिँदैछ । टोल–टोलमा सरसफाइ र फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउँदै हेटौँडालाई स्वच्छ, सुन्दर र पर्यटकमैत्री शहरका रूपमा विकास गर्ने र पर्यटन वर्षमा बढीभन्दा बढी पर्यटक भित्र्याउने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

articles.title: इन्सेन्टिभ वितरण नहुँदा सेवा ठप्प, मर्कामा सर्वसाधारण विरामी
articles.summary:
महोत्तरी । प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा सेवा लिन आउने नागरिक अनाहकमा पिडित बन्न पुगेका छन । मेडिकल सुपिरिटेंडेन्ट, अस्पताल संचालन तथा व्यस्थापन् समिति अध्यक्ष बिचको तालमेल समस्या र भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको बाकी इन्सेन्टिभ जस्ता आन्तरिक विवादका कारण सेवाग्राहीलाई मर्का परिरहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरमा अस्पतालमा भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा बन्द भएपछि बिरामीहरू निजी स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा महँगो शुल्क तिरेर सेवा लिन बाध्य छन् । अस्पताल प्रशासनले प्राविधिक कारणले सेवा वन्द रहेको सूचना टॉस गरि सेवा अवरुद्ध रहेको बताएको छ । तर भित्री कुरा भने भिडियो एक्सरे गर्ने चिकित्सकलाई इन्सेन्टिभ उपलब्ध नगराइएका कारण सो सेवा विगत दुई हप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि वन्द रहेको छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवले इन्सेन्टिभकै समस्याको कारणले दुईहप्ताभन्दा बढी समयदेखि भिडियो एक्सरे सेवा सुचारू हुन नसकेको स्विकारे । आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२\०८३ मा चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएका कारण सेवा वन्द गरेको बताउदै समस्या समाधानको पहल गरिरहेको निमित्त कार्यालय प्रमुख डा.रवि श्रीवास्तवको भनाइ छ ।

प्रादेशिक अस्पताल जलेश्वरका अस्पताल सञ्चालन तथा व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष रोहित प्रसाद ठाकुरले पनि काम गर्ने चिकित्सकहरुलाई इन्सेन्टिभ नदिएकै कारणले सेवा अवरुद्ध भएको बताए । उनले सेवा सुचारुको पहल गरिरहेको बताउदै अस्पताल व्यवस्थापन समितिको जेठ २८ गते बसेको बैठकले इन्सेन्टिभ दिने निर्णय गरेपनि सो किन वितरण गरिएन ? आशंका छन् ।

स्वास्थ सेवा जस्तो संवेदनशील संस्थाले अस्पतालको आन्तरिक तथा प्रशासनिक समस्याकै कारण सेवा ठप्प पार्नु, आम नागरिकलाई अनाहकमा समस्या दिनु स्वभाविक रुपमा लिन सकिदैन्। तर, यसको समाधान कसरी होला? सर्वसाधारणले नै सोध्न थालेका छन् ।

articles.title: देश धान्ने क्षेत्रमै संकट, श्रमिक विदेश पठाउन बन्द !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । वैदेशिक रोजगारीबाट आउने रेमिट्यान्सले देशको अर्थतन्त्र धान्न सहयोग पु¥याइरहेका म्यानपावर व्यवसायीले सरकारविरुद्ध दबाब बढाएका छन् । १५ बुँदे माग अघि सार्दै नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले शुक्रवारदेखि वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द गर्ने घोषणा गरेको छ । व्यवसायीहरूले नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म कामदार नपठाउने अडान लिएका छन् ।

नेपाल वैदेशिक रोजगार व्यवसायी संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार क्षेत्रका नीतिगत समस्या समाधान नभएको भन्दै शुक्रवारदेखि श्रमिक विदेश पठाउने कार्य पूर्ण रूपमा स्थगित गरेको छ । काठमाडौँमा पत्रकार सम्मेलन गर्दै संघले रेमिट्यान्सले मुलुकको अर्थतन्त्रमा ठूलो योगदान पु¥याए पनि सरकारले समयानुकूल नीति सुधार नगर्दा व्यवसायी र श्रमिक दुवै प्रभावित भएको जनाएको छ ।

संघले वैदेशिक रोजगार ऐन–२०६४ लाई समयसापेक्ष संशोधन, पारदर्शी लागत निर्धारण, वैज्ञानिक सेवा शुल्क, श्रमिक लक्षित गन्तव्य मुलुकको हवाई भाडा घटाउने तथा कृत्रिम अभाव अन्त्य गर्न माग गरेको छ । युरोपका नयाँ श्रम बजार, दक्षिण कोरियाको ई–सेभेन भिसा, जापानको ईएसडी कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन, महिला घरेलु कामदारका लागि नयाँ गन्तव्य खुला गर्ने र विभिन्न मुलुकमा देखिएका प्रशासनिक तथा बिचौलिया समस्या कूटनीतिक पहलमार्फत समाधान गर्नुपर्ने माग पनि अघि सारिएको छ ।

संघले मागपत्र प्रमाणीकरण र श्रम स्वीकृतिलाई पूर्ण रूपमा स्वचालित बनाउन, ५ हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली श्रमिक रहेका मुलुकमा श्रम सहचारी तथा काउन्सिलर नियुक्त गर्न, व्यवसायीले राखेको धरौटीको ब्याज उपलब्ध गराउन र श्रमिकलाई बिना धितो सहुलियतपूर्ण कर्जा दिने व्यवस्था गर्न पनि सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ । अध्यक्ष खत्रीले विशेष परिस्थितिमा सरकारकै निर्णय कार्यान्वयन गर्दा व्यवसायीमाथि कारबाही गरिएको आरोप लगाउँदै अब नीतिगत सुधार नभएसम्म श्रमिक नपठाउने स्पष्ट चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

संघले आफ्ना सबै माग सम्बोधन नभएसम्म शून्य समय घोषणा गर्दै वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा श्रमिक पठाउने सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रिया बन्द रहने जनाएको छ । व्यवसायीहरूको यो निर्णयले वैदेशिक रोजगारीमा जान तयारी गरिरहेका हजारौं नेपाली श्रमिक प्रत्यक्ष प्रभावित हुने देखिएको छ ।

articles.title: In Nepal, bankers are learning to fear the loan
articles.summary:
In September 2019, the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) of Nepal Police arrested 11 employees of the then Bank of Kathmandu, now merged with Global IME Bank Limited, including its then chief executive officer, accusing them of extending a loan secured by riverbed land as collateral. The case was decided three years ago. Borrower Surendra Shrestha was convicted, while the bank’s CEO and ten other employees were acquitted. The case is now before the Supreme Court.

In another case, the CIB investigated and filed a banking offence case in December 2025 against former Prabhu Bank chair Devi Prakash Bhattchan, former CEO Ashok Sherchan and other employees over transactions between Prabhu Bank and Prabhu Money Transfer, a remittance company. Nepal Rastra Bank, the country’s central bank and banking regulator, had conducted a “special inspection” of Prabhu Bank just three months before the arrest. The central bank had not identified an offence in the transactions in question, while the subsequent police investigation found serious irregularities and led to criminal charges.

A similar question has arisen over a loan extended by Nepal Investment Mega Bank to the now defunct Smart Telecom.

On January 14, 2020, Smart Telecom signed a loan agreement with the bank’s Kalimati branch to finance letters of credit for the import of telecommunications infrastructure. The total loan facility amounted to Rs5.82 billion and included overdraft, term loan, letter of credit, bills-bank guarantee and short-term loan.

Smart Telecom secured the loans against its machinery and equipment. After ownership of the pledged machinery and equipment passed to the government, the bank initiated a collateral auction to recover its outstanding dues. The transfer followed the revocation of Smart Telecom’s license after it failed to pay its dues to the government and renew the licence in 2023.

The CIB has now investigated the transaction and filed a case. Nepal Rastra Bank, however, has not publicly commented on the matter.

Former finance minister and former governor Yubaraj Khatiwada said Nepal Rastra Bank should be the first to examine such matters because it is the regulator of the financial sector.

“Every regulator has its own role in overseeing lending,” he said. “In the financial system, that responsibility lies with Nepal Rastra Bank,” he said.

These are not isolated cases. Police have stepped up investigations into loans extended by banks, even as the central bank says its regular supervision and regulatory inspections have not found the same irregularities. As a result, some bankers have been arrested while others are facing criminal cases.

The central bank’s silence has raised questions about its supervisory role. While bank CEOs and employees have faced arrest and prosecution, there has been no similar scrutiny of the officials responsible for overseeing those institutions.

The Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 2017 (BAFIA), requires banks to recover principal and interest by selling collateral when a borrower defaults or fails to pay interest or penalties. Banks have relied on this provision to justify auctioning collateral — the CIB, however, has questioned the process by which some of those assets were sold.

At a meeting with Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle last week, the CEOs of 20 commercial banks raised concerns that bankers could face arrest simply for decisions made in the course of lending.

Santosh Koirala, president of the Nepal Bankers’ Association, said bankers were increasingly fearful about being arrested despite following legal procedures and completing all required documentation when extending credit.

“There is a great deal of fear that we could be arrested simply for extending loans or making investments. The government needs to assure us that we can lend confidently and that it will stand by us if problems arise,” Koirala told the finance minister.

The auction of Smart Telecom's assets by Nepal Investment Mega Bank is the latest case to heighten that fear, Koirala said. “Investors were already worried that their investments could go bad because of the economic slowdown. Now bankers are worried that they could face government investigations or arrest simply for having extended those loans,” he said.

Regulator’s role questioned

Nara Bahadur Thapa, a former executive director of Nepal Rastra Bank, said it was inappropriate for the police and other government agencies to investigate banks and financial institutions that fall under the central bank’s regulatory jurisdiction.

“Agencies other than Nepal Rastra Bank should not intervene in investigations of banks and financial institutions,” Thapa said.

A report on the Prabhu Bank case by two NRB deputy directors, Krishna Sharan Phuyal and Maniraj Shrestha, assigned to assist the CIB investigation concluded that the company had mobilised funds from sources other than the amount invested by its own shareholders to operate its business.

Deependra Bahadur Kshetry, former governor, said the police investigation into Nepal Investment Mega Bank and other banks, and the arrests carried out in connection with those investigations, were inappropriate.

“Police had previously arrested CEO Jyoti Prakash Pandey as well. He was later released following a court order. Now the police have moved against the board of directors itself,” Kshetry said.

Nepal Rastra Bank has not publicly commented on the Smart Telecom loan, but it has sought clarification from the bank over the lending and recovery process. Nepal Investment Mega Bank submitted its response on April 27.

According to the bank, then Nepal Investment Bank, now Nepal Investment Mega Bank, and Prime Commercial Bank jointly extended loans to Smart Telecom under a consortium lending arrangement.

The loans, which were extended from fiscal year 2017-18 onwards, were secured against telecommunications equipment and other assets related to Smart Telecom’s operations. Most of those assets had been imported through letters of credit issued by the bank. The bank says the machinery and equipment were hypothecated under a deed registered at the Secured Transaction Registry Office, as required by law.

The loans remained performing for some time. After Smart Telecom failed to make its scheduled payments, however, the banks began recovery proceedings.

Invoking Section 57 of BAFIA, the bank published a 35-day notice on August 8, 2025, asking the borrower to settle its outstanding loan.

When Smart Telecom failed to repay within the stipulated period, the company itself wrote to the bank on September 5, 2025, asking it to auction the secured assets and recover the outstanding amount.

The bank subsequently published a 15-day public auction notice on September 19.

Three companies submitted applications. According to the bank, Axiata-owned Ncell was selected in accordance with the law and purchased the assets on October 6, 2025.

The bank acknowledges that it reached an understanding with Ncell regarding the purchase before publishing the auction notice.

Pramod Acharya, information officer at Nepal Investment Bank, said it was normal for a bank to identify potential buyers before putting collateral up for auction.

“If a potential buyer is not identified, there is no guarantee that applications will come simply because an advertisement has been published in a newspaper. Finding potential buyers is a normal practice when auctioning collateral,” he said.

The police, however, have treated that arrangement as evidence of collusion and are investigating it.

The CIB’s 2019 arrest of then Bank of Kathmandu employees was initiated after the bank itself asked the bureau to investigate its lending process.The bank had extended a loan against riverbed land as collateral. The CIB subsequently filed a case at the high court alleging banking offences and forgery.

A former Bank of Kathmandu employee named in that 2019 case said the verdict offered little redress for the years of anxiety and reputational harm they had suffered.

“When you work in a bank’s credit department, a loan goes through multiple layers of scrutiny. Different employees review and sign off on the file depending on the size and nature of the loan, before it is approved by the branch manager and ultimately the CEO,” the former employee said. “Not everyone involved in a process this complex can be presumed to have criminal intent. Yet the police treat everyone as equally culpable, leaving people like me to bear the consequences of an injustice.”

Former governor Chiranjibi Nepal said police have the legal authority to investigate banking offences, but criticised the growing practice of arresting bankers as if they were hardened criminals.

“Bankers should not be treated like criminals or murderers and subjected to arbitrary arrest. There should be a proper investigation and sufficient evidence before anyone is taken into custody,” Nepal said.

“What happens when someone’s reputation is ruined, their accounts are frozen, and their business activities are restricted, only to be cleared in the end? There is no way to fully undo the damage,” Nepal said.

Arresting bankers merely for extending loans could make them reluctant to lend in the future, Nepal warned. Banks could become particularly wary of financing projects that might eventually come under government ownership, potentially worsening liquidity problems in the financial system.

“Credit expansion in the banking sector is already weak. This case will further reduce the likelihood of banks financing large projects because banks have a legal right to recover loans,” he said.

Legally, the police do not have that authority. The Banking Offence and Punishment Act classifies banking offences as state cases, prosecuted by the government rather than private parties (Section 18); allows police to detain suspects and form specialised investigation teams (Section 19); and requires banks to cooperate with investigations (Section 20).

Superintendent of Police, Anupam Shamsher JBR, spokesperson for the CIB, said the bureau investigates banking offences on the basis of complaints from Nepal Rastra Bank, banks and financial institutions, as well as individuals. “The police have the authority to investigate banking offences under BAFIA, the Banking Offence and Punishment Act and several other laws,” Rana told Kantipur.

He said the CIB had completed its investigation into the alleged illegal auction of Smart Telecom’s assets, which are now under government ownership, and submitted its investigation report to the Kathmandu District Government Attorney’s Office.

“We completed the investigation in accordance with the law and submitted the report. A case was filed on Wednesday. The claimed loss is Rs95 billion and 22 people have been named as defendants,” Rana said.

The police allege that Nepal Investment Bank and Ncell colluded to carry out an unlawful auction and that the case involves fraud, criminal breach of trust and organised crime.

Asked whether the CIB is required to inform Nepal Rastra Bank when investigating banking offences, Rana said the regulator is involved when necessary. “We do not keep Nepal Rastra Bank in the dark. Experts with knowledge of the banking sector are brought in from the central bank when necessary. So the central bank is informed as required,” he said.

A police source said the investigation into the loan recovery process involving Investment Bank and Smart Telecom was launched following instructions from the government, including the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, on three grounds: a letter from that office and the report of a committee headed by former attorney general Tankamani Sharma, which investigated the purchase and sale of Ncell’s shares in 2023; an application filed with the police by Usha Pradhan, the landlord of the premises occupied by Smart Telecom, seeking recovery of rent through the bank; and an alleged BAFIA violation covering irregularities in lending, collateral valuation, and loan recovery — including assigning an artificial value when auctioning collateral or accepting non-banking assets.

The report of the study and investigation committee led by Sharma, which examined the purchase and sale of Ncell shares, also specifically recommended that Nepal Rastra Bank investigate loans extended by banks and financial institutions to telecommunications companies. It made no mention of police involvement.

“Given that banks and financial institutions appear to have created financial risks by extending unusually large funded and non-funded loans to Nepali telecommunications service providers, including Ncell Axiata, Smart Telecom and Sunivera Capital Ventures, Nepal Rastra Bank should conduct further investigation in relation to the banks and financial institutions,” the report said.

A central bank official maintained that they are unaware of the police investigations. “In many cases, experts from Nepal Rastra Bank are assigned to the CIB investigation team,” he said. “In some investigations where no expert is assigned, there are discussions between the police and the governor or senior officials of the central bank. But those discussions are informal.”

Sudha Shrestha, NRB’s deputy spokesperson, said the central bank has the primary responsibility for investigating loans extended by banks and financial institutions.

“Nepal Rastra Bank should examine such matters first,” she said. “But in some cases, complaints are filed directly with the police, or other state cases may also involve loan transactions. In such situations, the police may conduct their own investigation, but they also coordinate closely with Nepal Rastra Bank.”

She added the central bank was aware of the dispute over the Smart Telecom auction.

“Nepal Rastra Bank is seeking legal advice on the auction of Smart Telecom’s collateral,” she said.

articles.title: Back in Nepal, Deuba seeks to reclaim Congress leadership
articles.summary:
Dispute in the Nepali Congress has taken a new turn after leaders close to former president Sher Bahadur Deuba proposed accepting him as party president and holding the 15th general convention under his leadership.

The proposal follows the Supreme Court’s decision to allow a review of its April 17 verdict recognising the Gagan Thapa-led Congress panel as the legitimate party leadership. The Deuba faction now says there are two options: wait for the court’s final ruling or agree to hold the general convention under Deuba.

“We can either wait for the court’s final verdict or accept the central working committee elected under Sher Bahadur Deuba’s leadership from the 14th general convention and go to the general convention,” said Prakash Sharan Mahat, a leader close to Deuba.

“Naturally, Sher Bahadur Deuba should conduct the 15th general convention. There was an accident in between in the name of a special convention. Now that the Supreme Court has agreed to review its earlier decision, if the other side is ready to hold the general convention under Sher Bahadur Deuba’s leadership, there is no need to wait for the final verdict. Unity can be achieved in the meantime.”

Mahat said Deuba’s leadership would make it easier to accommodate rival groups. “Everyone can come together under Sher Bahadur Deuba’s leadership. No one will be favoured or sidelined,” he said.

The proposal is a shift from the Deuba camp’s earlier position. Before the review was allowed, its leaders had been preparing a gathering that some said could lead to a new party if the court upheld Thapa’s leadership.

The court’s decision has ended the immediate prospect of a split, but has not settled the dispute. Deuba-aligned leaders are holding a gathering from Friday to Sunday at the Miracle Party Venue in Kathmandu. Any decision from the meeting on reconciliation or separation could shape the next phase of the crisis.

Deuba, the five-time prime minister and Congress president for two terms, returned to Nepal on Thursday after about five months abroad. He travelled directly from the airport to the contact office of his faction at Chundevi, where leaders and cadres had gathered. At their request, he briefly addressed them and rejected allegations including financial irregularities levelled against him.

Suggesting the hollowness of accusations, including political charges against him during the partyless Panchayat era, the direct rule of King Gyanendra and the latest period of the Rastriya Swatantra Party government led by Balendra Shah, Deuba said, “King Gyanendra could not do it; can anyone else do it here?”

Before reaching Chundevi, Deuba had issued an appeal for an end to disagreement and dissatisfaction within the Congress. Warning that the dispute in the country’s democratic party could weaken national unity, he urged leaders, cadres, supporters, well-wishers and voters to move ahead by respecting the sacrifices and struggles.

Deuba also said young leaders should move forward in Congress politics, while warning against portraying experienced politicians as worthless and allowing a leader’s social-media fame to take over party responsibilities.

The dispute stems from the special general convention held in January. The convention, demanded by more than 40 percent of the general convention delegates, elected Thapa as president. After the Election Commission recognised the Thapa-led committee, the Deuba faction challenged that decision in the Supreme Court.

On April 17, a division bench of the court recognised the Thapa faction as the official Nepali Congress, ending a three-month dispute over leadership. The court upheld the Election Commission’s recognition of the Thapa-led committee and validated its decisions.

The Deuba faction then sought a review, arguing that the verdict was flawed legally. The Supreme Court registered the petition on July 22 after a preliminary examination. Its decision to allow the review has reopened the legal question over party leadership.

General Secretary Pradip Paudel rejected the proposal to restore Deuba as president. “There is no question of going to the general convention by accepting again as president the leadership displaced through the lawful process of the special general convention. That does not make sense legally, procedurally or politically,” said Paudel.

He said Deuba, who has already served two terms as party president, should remain above the factional contest and play a guardian-like role for the broader unity of the party. “We had hoped he would correct the situation saying, ‘I am not the president, so do not call me the president.’ We still believe he will take the initiative for unity.”

Thapa welcomed Deuba’s return at the beginning of Thursday’s Central Working Committee meeting. “Former president Sher Bahadur Deuba had gone abroad for medical treatment. He has returned after recovering, and I warmly welcome him [back],” said Thapa.

The Congress statute provides a four-year term for the Central Working Committee, with a possible one-year extension. Paudel warned that failing to hold the convention within the given period could put the party in a difficult spot. Leaders close to Deuba argue that the constitution allows additional time.

The previous central working committee had set October 2 to 5 for the general convention, Paudel said, adding that the schedule would remain in place, with only some dates for lower-level conventions adjusted.

The Deuba camp has indicated that it could knock on the Supreme Court’s door if the Thapa-led leadership proceeded with the convention on a “premature” date.

“If the Supreme Court issues a stay order, everyone will have no option but to wait for the final verdict,” said a Congress leader close to Deuba. “If it does not, we will hold a separate convention. Then congress will then split into two.”

The leadership crisis has been compounded by Deuba’s legal troubles. While he was abroad, the Department of Money Laundering Investigation pursued an investigation involving his family. Deuba and his wife, former foreign minister Arzu Rana Deuba, had been issued arrest warrants from the Kathmandu District Court.

The Supreme Court on May 25 directed the authorities not to arrest the Deuba couple, ruling that the warrants had no legal validity. It said offences investigated by the Department of Money Laundering Investigation fall under the Special Court’s jurisdiction and that sufficient legal grounds for arrest had not been established. Interpol also declined to issue a Red Notice against the couple.

The money-laundering investigation continues. In July, investigators filed a chargesheet at the Special Court detailing a Rs26 million transaction involving companies owned by Deuba’s son, Jayabir Deuba.

Deuba’s personal secretary Bhanu Deuba said there had been no discussion yet on how the former prime minister would respond to the investigation following his return.

articles.title: It’s annual baby boom season at Nepal’s maternity hospitals
articles.summary:
For Nepal’s maternity hospitals, this is the busiest time of year.

As many as 142 women gave birth through normal delivery at Thapathali-based Paropakar Maternity and Women’s Hospital on Tuesday, while another 42 delivered by caeserean section. On Wednesday 102 women had normal deliveries and 28 had caeserean section.

Both figures are more than double the hospital’s usual daily number of deliveries.

Doctors and health workers at the hospital say the rise is not unusual. Every year, from mid-June to mid-September, the delivery rate increases significantly.

“Come to our hospital to see the patient flow,” said Dr Shanti Shrestha, senior consultant gynaecologist and obstetrician at the hospital. “Deliveries have started, and we are very busy.”

Due to an increase in the number of pregnant women seeking delivery services, all beds at the hospital have been occupied, and the hospital administration has been accommodating two new mothers in a single bed.

“We can’t turn away women who are in labour,” said Dr Shree Prasad Adhikari, director at the hospital. “Adjusting two patients in a single bed is not our choice, but an initiative we have taken to save the lives of new mothers and their babies.”

Doctors say the hospital sees a seasonal rise in deliveries from mid-June to mid-September, a period health workers call the delivery season. Normally, around 50 women give birth at the hospital each day. In recent weeks, however, daily deliveries have more than doubled on some days, and exceeded 90 on other days.

According to hospital data, 1,540 women gave birth in Baisakh (mid April-mid May), and 1,569 women in Jestha (mid May-mid June). The number increased to 1,880 in Asar (mid June-mid July). Similarly, in Chaitra (mid March-mid April), 1,452 women gave birth at the hospital.

In the month of Shrawan (mid-July to mid-August) of the last fiscal year, 2025-26, a total of 1,948 women gave birth at the hospital, while the number was 2,141 in the fiscal year 2024-025.

Adhikari said that his hospital has set up a separate observation ward to accommodate the growing number of patients.

“Women in early stages of labour or those who are not yet ready to deliver, sometimes have to share a bed,” said Adhikari. “Once labour progresses and they are ready to give birth, they are moved to the delivery room.”

The surge is not limited to Kathmandu. Hospitals in the districts are also seeing a rise in the number of women seeking delivery services.

At the Chitwan-based Bharatpur Hospital, for example, the number of deliveries has risen significantly in recent days.

“Normally, around 25 women used to seek delivery services in our hospital a day,” said Professor Sunil Mani Pokhrel, head of the gynaecology department of the hospital. “These days the number has risen to more than 40. We have been struggling to manage the beds.”

Doctors expect the number of deliveries to remain high until October. They link the seasonal rise with Nepal’s main wedding season (Mangsir, Magh, Falgun) or December through February).

Those who conceive in December usually give birth in August, those who conceive in January give birth in September, and those who conceive in February give birth in October.

“Apart from that, migrant workers, especially youths, who are abroad for employment return home during the festive season, especially Dashain and Tihar, which falls in October,” said Dr Pawan Sharma, a consultant gynaecologist. “Many couples conceive babies during this period. These days, many youths also return home planning to have a baby.”

Doctors say the chances of conception increases when young couples spend more time together and do not use contraceptives. The festive season, when people tend to relax and spend more time together, can therefore contribute to an increase in conceptions, they say.

articles.title: Paras Khadka on leadership shift, squad depth and Nepal’s cricket roadmap
articles.summary:
Following the Cricket Association of Nepal’s decision to restructure the national team’s leadership—appointing Sandeep Lamichhane as ODI captain and Dipendra Singh Airee as T20I captain, effectively ending Rohit Kumar Paudel’s five-year tenure—questions have surfaced regarding team stability, selection autonomy, and Nepal’s campaign in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2.

At the TU International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur, Sabina Karki caught up with CAN Secretary and former national team captain Paras Khadka on Thursday to discuss the rationale behind the captaincy overhaul, the independence of the selection committee, and the road ahead for Nepali cricket.

Sandeep Lamichhane has replaced Rohit Paudel at the helm of the ODI team. What was the core reason behind this decision from CAN’s perspective?

Rohit stepped into the leadership role during a very sensitive period around four years ago and did a remarkable job. Captaincy is evaluated on many parameters, but his dedication, integrity and work ethic in taking the team forward make CAN, the fans, and everyone involved in Nepali cricket—including myself personally—extremely proud of him.

However, change is an inevitable part of sports. Whether a decision proves right or wrong is something history will judge, but within the board, we felt that the burden of captaincy was impacting Rohit’s personal batting performance. After about four years at the helm, we wanted to give him the freedom to focus on his game as a player. Furthermore, moving forward, we wanted to explore new leadership dynamics to see if we could cultivate a fresh playing style.

This wasn’t a knee-jerk reaction to losing four consecutive matches in CWC League-2. It was an ongoing internal discussion involving assistant coaches, team managers, support staff, active and non-active players, the selection committee and the board. While respecting Rohit’s immense contribution, we felt it was time for a structural shift. He still has a long career ahead and plenty more to contribute to Nepal.

Was Rohit Paudel consulted before the decision was finalised? How did he receive the news?

To put things in perspective, when I was appointed captain to replace Binod Das, nobody gave me advance notice—it was simply announced. That said, we strive for open communication with our players.

When we made the T20I captaincy change earlier to appoint Dipendra Singh Airee, Rohit was informed beforehand. For this ODI transition, our management communicated the shift to him, and I reached out to him personally via text as well.

The underlying reality is that our overall growth had felt somewhat stagnant. If you look at Nepal's home record from 2020 through 2026, it is phenomenal across all leadership tenures. But away from home, we have consistently struggled. Over the last four to five years, the same core group of 15 to 20 players has been rotated across every format. While this group took us to the Asia Cup and the World Cup, sticking strictly to the same pool without introducing fresh competition was holding us back.

Critics often allege that CAN management interferes heavily in team selection and that the selection committee lacks independence. How autonomous is the selection process?

Following LB Chhetri’s resignation around the 2026 T20 World Cup, the selection panel has been functioning with Yunil Shrestha and Murtuja Haware. Nearly 97 to 98 percent of the time, the final squad selected is the exact team requested by the head coach and captain in coordination with the selection panel.

There is a distinction between selecting a squad and changing national captaincy. Historically, appointing or changing a national captain is a direct board decision made after evaluating broad feedback from coaches, managers, and support staff—it is not solely a selection committee call.

When I captained the national team for ten years, there was zero board interference in squad selection; the captain and coach sat down with selectors to finalise the team. That culture remains intact. The board’s involvement here was specifically regarding the overarching strategic decision on captaincy.

Dipendra Singh Airee was the ODI vice-captain and was recently handed the T20I leadership. Many expected him to take over the ODI team as well. Why appoint Sandeep Lamichhane specifically for ODIs instead of having a single captain across formats?

We wanted two distinct perspectives for two different formats. When a single leadership mindset governs all formats, domestic performers and emerging players end up getting very limited opportunities, despite CAN’s heavy investment in grassroots cricket.

By appointing Dipendra for T20Is and Sandeep for ODIs, each captain, together with the head coach and selectors, will independently identify the best 15 players required for their respective formats.

In professional cricket, accountability is essential. If you don't score runs or pick wickets, you have to step aside. Splitting the leadership forces healthy internal competition, broadens our talent pool, and ensures that playing for the national team remains earned through consistent performance.

Nepal’s ODI status is under severe pressure with only four matches remaining in the current CWC League 2 cycle and a playoff spot looming. Is CAN confident that these squad overhauls will help retain ODI status?

ODI cricket is not easy. In this cycle alone, we lost five or six close matches by margins of just two or three runs. It isn't that we lack a good team, but rather that we have historically been in a 'management phase' rather than a true structural 'development phase'.

We are realistically preparing for the CWC playoffs. Instead of throwing inexperienced players into high-stakes playoff matches without preparation, we are using the upcoming fixtures—including the ACC Premier Cup and our tour to Australia featuring Top End T20 and three 50-over games—to test combinations. We will have around 12 matches prior to the crucial League-2 fixtures to evaluate who earns a spot in the primary 15-man squad.

If we want to transition from merely surviving in ODI cricket to becoming the top Associate nation, creating squad competition and giving young players international exposure right now is vital.

There are persistent rumours that CAN is also considering changes to the head coach and support staff. Is there any truth to this?

No, for now, I think we should stick to the next tours. Modern-day cricket has changed. Because unlike in the past, if a player says they will play for 10, 12, or 15 years, it might be rare. If a player has a period—whether it's six months or two years—we need to identify where they can give their best. And at that point, who are the decision-makers? In our cricket team, again, it's the coach and the captain that decide who plays and almost who gets selected in the 15.

So putting all those things together, for now, we are—let's say—we just made the change in captaincy. Regarding the coach, it has barely been a year since he arrived. We have evaluated him as well and taken feedback from everyone, including teams, especially the players.

Decisions aren't made solely on wins or losses. For instance, our previous coach, Monty Desai, delivered incredible results by winning 11 out of 12 ODIs in his first year, but won only 2 out of 10 the following year, leading to his change after gathering everyone's feedback. Our decision-making evaluates on-field performance alongside off-field factors, including the code of conduct, teamwork, and the broader framework. For now, we are focusing on the captaincy transition—resting a few players while giving young and existing players a chance to prove themselves and foster healthy competition. While we are currently only changing the captain, if the situation requires it, we are fully prepared to make changes to the coach and captain, because even the board itself gets changed timely.

Finally, speaking not as CAN Secretary but as a former national captain, what do you expect from Sandeep in this new role?

ODI cricket is important, ODI status is important, but now we need to move into a development phase. Sandeep is one of our leading performers, and this is an opportunity for him to inspire others and bring the team together, building team spirit and bonding.

Rather than asking whether ODI cricket survives under Sandeep’s captaincy, the question should be whether Nepal cricket can retain its ODI status. Everyone has to support the captain on the field. Nepal cricket is bigger than any individual.

We all want to help the team win, and we all want to grow as a cricketing nation together. We have to go beyond ODI status. The quality of players we have can save our status. But going beyond that, we need to create a better cricketing environment in the country.

On a different topic, regarding this discussion currently taking place among Associate nations about the ODI World Cup format pathway, Scotland and Netherlands have already expressed their dissatisfaction, haven't they? What is CAN's stand on that?

When Bangladesh did not qualify for the World Cup, Scotland got a direct entry into the World Cup, right? I think ICC did that as well. Normally, direct entry doesn't happen in World Cups.

Obviously, there have been many discussions about the ODI cricket format, and coordination among ODI nations has taken place. But for that, there are also representatives of Associate nations, who were recently selected from the AGM, and after the ODI status format came out, there has been a lot of discussion underneath regarding what should happen.

First, we have to recognise the commercial reality of modern cricket. The ICC is prioritising the T20 format to expand the game globally because it generates strong commercial returns—granting T20I status to all international matches was a key part of that strategy. While we all want more teams in 50-over cricket, expanding ODIs to 18–20 nations involves heavy broadcast and operational costs that require massive financial backing.

As for the statements from Scotland and the Netherlands, that is their independent board decision. At CAN, we prefer working through official channels. Nepal helped elect three Associate representatives to the ICC Chief Executives' Committee (CEC) who coordinate directly with the ICC CEO and Board. Rather than issuing public complaints, we rely on our designated CEC representatives to raise our structural concerns directly at the decision-making table.

Finally, where have the preparations for NPL reached, and now, right from before the season starts, there was this question of whether we will get ICC's sanction, whether we get T20 recognition or not—what is the status as this season arrives?

It's true people say CAN is solely focused on the NPL and T20s, but the NPL is a marquee tournament. It commands higher investment, massive interest, and has built a distinct international profile for Nepali cricket. Having successfully delivered two editions through immense hard work, the operational preparation is now moving forward naturally. We’ve taken extensive steps with the ICC regarding official sanction and recognition, and we are awaiting good news.

But our focus extends far beyond just the NPL. The next 10 months are crucial for Nepali cricket—we are hosting the U19 Women's T20 World Cup, preparing for the CWC League-2 playoffs, running the NPL, and hosting the India 'A' series. Because we have to manage multiple major tournaments simultaneously, our immediate priority is executing the NPL while finalising our broader policies and next year's cricketing calendar to deliver an even higher standard across all formats.

articles.title: Make inclusion a reality, not rhetoric
articles.summary:
When the Rastriya Swatantra Party came to power in March with a near two-thirds majority, Nepal, for the first time, saw roughly 35 percent women in the House of Representatives. Following this, Prime Minister Balendra Shah appointed six women ministers to his 17-member Cabinet. Even as ministers from the Khas-Arya dominate the ministry leadership, those from the Madheshi, Janajati and Dalit communities are also represented. For a country that has long struggled to place women in top leadership positions, the government’s move was historic and commendable. It also instilled hope that it would prioritise inclusivity in all vital appointments.

But beyond the Cabinet, the government’s appointments to constitutional bodies, commissions, universities and cultural institutions are far from inclusive. Between March 27 and August 11, the Cabinet made more than 50 appointments, of which only four were women. Madheshis, Janajatis and Dalits were thinly represented; Muslims were entirely excluded. Similarly, there isn’t a single woman among the three appointments to the Election Commission; nor are there any people from the Madheshi community. This is a continuation of the disregard of inclusion by previous governments. Even in senior university appointments, the notion of inclusion has been flouted: The government recently appointed seven university vice-chancellors, but not a single woman made the list. Appointments to state-run cultural academies failed to reflect the country’s regional gap and ethnic diversity.

The government justifies the appointments as being based on merit and open competition. It is true that Nepal’s public institutions are in dire need of competent people and should be free from political patronage, but the Balendra Shah government must internalise the idea that excluding people from marginalised communities from vital positions entails exclusion of an array of diverse views, inviting criticisms that the state still views them as ‘incompetent’. These institutions cannot be run by a cluster of historically privileged groups, with a similar worldview.

The Constitution recognises inclusion as the fundamental principle of the state. Hence, it is also vital to ask: What does merit mean in a country where access to education, job opportunities and institutions has often sidelined women, Janajatis, Madheshis and Dalits? Centuries-old social hierarchies, such as the caste system, regional disparities and gender discrimination have resulted in structural inequality in Nepal. Underrepresented groups cannot remain marginalised because they lack sufficient representatives to work for their upliftment and representation. Nepal cannot afford to push them back further.

The current Cabinet is considered the youngest and most academically qualified in the country’s history. They have repeatedly promised not to repeat the political practices of old parties. Being transparent about recent appointments would be a good start, but that is not enough. What’s more vital is for them to understand that they should prioritise inclusion in key appointments not only to correct historical exclusion faced by marginalised communities and people from remote regions but also to ensure that those positions aren’t reserved for the privileged few. If they don’t correct their course, they will lose the confidence of the marginalised communities who also voted them to power. They must break the cycle of exclusion, just as they did in Parliament and the Cabinet.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s new political darling is losing its spark
articles.summary:
For quite a long time, Nepalis had no option but to vote in conformity with their old political fan clubs, merely serving their own interests rather than the greater good. They never fostered bigger dreams. After long-serving, tested politicians failed to perform better, ‘change’ became a buzzword throughout the nation. Fueled by public anger and frustration, some urban and suburban Nepalis formed an ideologically unanchored party in 2022 and called it Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), which translates to National Independent Party—practically implying freedom from any old political doctrines.

The new party mesmerised the public with hype and charm, deploying a set of fresh faces in national media after a long time. The RSP brand quickly became the talk of the town, especially in the middle-class segments of rural and urban Nepal.

As a reaction to aggressive gerontocracy in almost all institutional domains and particularly to the social media ban imposed by the UML government, Nepal witnessed a Gen Z revolt on September 8-9, 2025. The uprising resulted in the bloodshed of 76 Nepalis all over the country, with an estimated Rs85 billion worth of loss. The aftermath of the Gen Z movement further exacerbated the need for urgent change in mainstream politics, threatening the shares of political power of the old parties—the Nepali Congress, the UML and the Maoists (now NCP). This led to a call for a snap election in the country, putting the RSP brand in an advantageous position.

The RSP alone was unable to encash this situation as they were not fully able to imbibe the spirit of the Gen Z movement owing to their fragile ideological and methodological standing. So, a significant space was provided to the urban elites who somehow managed to show their faces and create viral, decent political reels during the movement.

Enter the viral part-time rapper, full-time Mayor of Nepal’s biggest metropolis Balendra Shah in the RSP show.

Shah, hailing from the Madheshi community and with approximately 58 percent of the total national votes coming from Madhesh province, was a sound marketing strategy for RSP’s PM candidacy. His candidacy also stood for political revenge against prevailing gerontocracy dominance. The new ‘Balen’ flagship featured in the RSP brand sent ripples in the public sphere. The party eventually won 182 of 275 HoR seats—a landslide victory. Yet the possibility of a new sound turning into a melody now seems probable.

Irrespective of government changes, for the Nepali middle-class, the question of accessible quality education, health, food and energy has always been the wolf at the door. As RSP is an embodiment of middle-class thought, it is shackled to fulfil the very economic and political aspirations of its major voters. Ironically, the party is not ready to listen to the rising middle-class cries—rising commuting charges, burgeoning rent, fuel and energy prices, and midnight hustle for cooking gases, just to name a few. And, mind you, blaming external shocks for these signals of economic havoc would betray the middle class twice, inviting mistrust in the party.The mistrust loop it invites seems complex. Investors are unable to regain their confidence, whereas consumers now fear spending. The father of capitalism, Adam Smith, says it is the ‘invisible hand’ that corrects the market. However, even the invisible hand seems to fail in Nepal’s economic landscape. Meanwhile, sitting RSP ministers suspect each move of the political actors, whether inside or outside the party. Such developments have not only confused the RSP’s core members but have also left its voters bewildered, unsure of what to make of the unfolding political fiasco.

The RSP’s 100-day plan, touted as the blueprint for immediate reform and cherished by the public initially, remains uncelebrated for failing to answer some important ‘wh’s: who benefits, who was intently excluded, and, importantly, who gets to decide? Technocracy, though not purely antithetical to democracy, creates hurdles when expertise starts substituting political deliberation. RSP’s technocratic illusion is becoming counterproductive to its integrity, with its technical correctness presented as political neutrality, leaving the agendas of distribution, priorities, recognition, and social justice aloof.

The gap between the RSP’s promise of transformation before the election and the governance experience now feels real. Everyday frustration is back to its norm, whether it be standing in long queues or paying extra rupees in bills. A layman is increasingly finding themself disillusioned with the RSP’s anti-establishment rhetoric, subtly reminding the regime of the persisting Nepali crisis of political faith. Such a situation not only adds to the public distrust, but a failure of populist promise may discredit RSP’s wanna-be Raghav Chadha or any ambitious ‘Ivy League netas’ and might spark a possibility of change which we Nepalis are tired of now.

The RSP, a politically neutral platform embracing significant influencers, is undoubtedly facing pressure to ‘look good’ in the eyes of Nepali society, be it inside or outside the country. This has been further illustrated by the duality of RSP parliamentarians on a plethora of regional and national issues. In democracies, questioning one’s own party is a healthy practice; it strengthens democratic values. However, the matter of integrity cannot be subjugated when it comes into the hands of the ruling party. In doing so, a ‘fit-in’ strategy might further escalate the doubt about conflicts of interest within the party and introduce another level of chaos.

Today, young Nepalis are unlearning faster than before. They desire more transparency, accountability, equity, inclusivity, ethical governance and fair participation. And the most beautiful thing is that we are learning how to start a dialogue to demand these desires in a much more responsible manner. The central idea of democracy is not to eliminate politics through expertise but to place expertise within political realms—subject to scrutiny, ideological and methodological orientation, accountability and public judgment. So, just in the name of ‘governance’, the impending issues on federalism, financial decentralisation, secularism, gender, inequality, informality, distribution, caste and social justice cannot be subdued. Though the RSP’s dream has seemingly become untrendy, these impending issues don’t easily erase themselves from public consciousness—the party has no excuses to ignore the writings on the walls.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s universities are straining to keep up with student demand
articles.summary:
It is difficult being an educator at a time when you continue to face complaints from employers that graduates are not job-ready. At the recently held panel discussion and workshop, this issue was once again raised. This is something I usually hear in conversations with employers as well as academics within and even outside my institution. I notice that it is rarely addressed as purely a matter of curriculum deficiency. It has increasingly become more of a human resource issue. Universities and Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) are short of qualified faculty who consistently impart the right content.

According to the University Grants Commission’s EMIS figures for 2023/24, 12,082 full-time teachers work in the constituent campuses. However, the community and private affiliated campuses, which enrol approximately 62 percent of the total 633,053 students enrolled in higher education institutions in Nepal, are not required to submit any full-time faculty register data. As a result, the actual picture of full-time faculty members cannot be easily estimated and is likely to be a fraction of what enrolment numbers would demand.

The disparity becomes distinct when one juxtaposes the trend lines of two different measures. From 2016/17 to 2023/24, overall higher education enrollment in Nepal increased by around 71 percent, growing from 371,000 to 633,000 students. In the same period, the teaching staff across the constituent campuses increased by less than 30 percent, from 9,299 to 12,082 faculty members. Students are now joining the educational system almost twice as fast as their instructors join to educate them.

The disparities between the universities are just as illustrative. Tribhuvan University, which accounts for more than 75 percent of the country’s higher education student body, reports a student-teacher ratio of around 21:1 within its constituent campuses. The ratio for Kathmandu University is about 25:1, for Far-Western University 47:1, and for Nepal Open University, whose distance learning model explains the huge numbers, the ratio is a rather striking 102:1. This suggests that teaching capacity is unevenly distributed by institution as well as by discipline.

The amount of public funding has also increased from Rs9.3 billion in 2017/18 to Rs17.5 billion in 2023/24, although most of this additional funding has been made in infrastructure and block grants rather than the recruitment of full-time faculty members, especially outside HEIs in Kathmandu.

When placed against international benchmarks, Nepal’s position appears to be dismal. The generally quoted planning range of the student-to-faculty ratio is 10:1 to 20:1 internationally. In the case of the United States, the average student-to-faculty ratio at degree-granting institutions was approximately 13:1 in the fall of 2022, 14:1 in public four-year colleges and 10:1 in private non-profit four-year colleges. The standards for AICTE of India for technical education regard the faculty-to-student ratio as 10:1 and 15:1 to be the minimum acceptable ratio for relevant technical courses due to the nature of laboratory-based courses.

According to UNESCO and the World Bank’s tertiary-level indicators, however, international comparisons of teacher-student ratio are clouded by varying definitions of ‘teacher’ and differential treatment of part-time teachers.
