articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: Man-made water hazards are becoming a deadly monsoon trap for children
articles.summary:
The monsoon brings the familiar threat of floods and inundation to Nepal’s southern plains. But for children, another danger is often closer to home: water collecting in pits, construction sites, open drains and unfinished infrastructure.

Roadside excavations, holes dug for brick kilns, ponds, irrigation canals and trenches around culverts and bridges can become deadly traps once filled with rainwater. The danger is often invisible. Children may have no way of judging how deep the water is before stepping in to play, bathe or swim.

Last Friday, 7-year-old Khushi Alam drowned in a water-filled pit beside a culvert in ward 5 of Yamunamai Rural Municipality, Rautahat district.

Khushi had gone to play with four or five friends at a culvert about a kilometre west of his home. His friends returned in the evening, but Khushi did not. When he failed to come home late into the night, relatives and neighbours began searching for him. His father reported him missing at a police post in Bamanhar.

Police eventually found Khushi’s body in a pit about 20 feet south of the culvert along the Satbamba road.

Ward chair Shivendra Sah said the pit had existed for years and had filled with rainwater.

“It is an old pit beside the road,” Sah said. “It is difficult to fill it, and it cannot simply be left as it is. Children are attracted to such water-filled pits, but the consequences are becoming serious.”

The ward has since conducted awareness programmes at schools and urged children to stay away from stagnant water.

Khushi’s death was far from an isolated case in Rautahat or the wider Madhesh province.

On July 28, two sisters, 5-year-old Puchki and 3-year-old Ghaghari, drowned in a water-filled excavation near an under-construction bridge in Chakradaha, in ward 26 of Birgunj Metropolitan City, Parsa district.

The girls, daughters of Prabhu Thakur of Sughauli, had gone to a field with their grandfather, Kishori Thakur. The family arrived at about 11am. Their grandfather left the children briefly while he went to call their grandmother. When he returned, the girls were gone.

Their family searched nearby and contacted relatives. Their mother, Antima Devi, reported them missing to the Sughauli Area Police Office that night. Police found both girls dead the following morning in the flooded pit near the bridge.

In Siraha district, three children from the same family died in another water-filled excavation on July 12.

The children, 12-year-old Sabnam Khatun, 10-year-old Rubina Khatun and 7-year-old Saiful Sheikh, drowned while bathing in a pit at a livestock market in Choharwa, ward 7 of Golbazar Municipality. Residents and security personnel pulled them from the water and took them to the hospital, where doctors pronounced all three dead.

Golbazar Mayor Shyam Kumar Shrestha said the pit had been there for years and was used as a water source for livestock.

“We never imagined such an incident could happen,” Shrestha said. “We will fence the area rather than fill the pit, as it is used like a pond for animals.”

He said the municipality would also run awareness campaigns.

In Mahottari district, three girls drowned on May 22 in the village of Sarpallo in ward 7 of Manarashiswa Municipality. The victims were 12-year-old Sneha Kumari and 6-year-old Shivani Kumari, daughters of Birendra Bhandari, and 12-year-old Afsana Khatun, daughter of Aziz Nadaf.

Police said the girls had gone swimming at the confluence of the Ankushi and Jangha rivers. They slipped while bathing and were swept into deeper water.

That same day, 2-year-old Deepika Kumari, daughter of Naresh Mahato, drowned in rainwater that had collected in a field near her home in Rajkhor village, ward 4 of Gaushala Municipality.

Mahottari Assistant Chief District Officer Sanjay Kumar Pokharel blamed a lack of public awareness for the recurring deaths.

“We repeatedly tell local governments at every disaster-management meeting to fill dangerous pits,” Pokharel said. “We even make policy decisions on the issue. But it is unclear whether elected representatives are ignoring them or what is happening.”

The incidents show that children are not drowning only in rivers, streams and natural water bodies. Water collecting in roadside pits, culverts, construction sites, farmland and old excavations around settlements can be just as deadly.

A recurring seasonal tragedy

The scale of drowning deaths among children in Madhesh is stark.

According to the Madhesh Province Police Office in Janakpur, 608 children have drowned in the province’s eight districts over the past seven fiscal years, from 2019-20.

Rautahat recorded the highest number, with 110 child deaths. Dhanusha reported 102, Siraha 81, Saptari 75, Mahottari 71, Bara 66, Sarlahi 60 and Parsa 43.

Police data show that many of the deaths do not occur in major rivers or natural lakes. Children are frequently killed in culverts, irrigation channels, deep pits excavated for brickmaking, ponds and roadside trenches.

The pattern points to a problem that extends beyond parental supervision.

Former Madhesh provincial assembly member Dhan Lal Thokar said poorly managed infrastructure and unsafe excavation were major contributors.

“Brick kilns, soil excavation sites and roadside culverts are routinely left open after construction,” Thokar said. “Villages often lack safe places for children to play, so they end up around water-filled pits and culverts. This is not simply an unfortunate accident or a failure of parental care.”

The problem is particularly acute around brick kilns, where deep pits are dug to extract soil and can later fill with rainwater.

Rautahat Chief District Officer Dinesh Sagar Bhusal said local units had repeatedly been asked to fill dangerous pits or secure them with fences and warning signs.

“We have told elected representatives again and again,” Bhusal said. “We are tired of repeating ourselves. Yet they simply do not act. It is becoming a serious problem.”

He said brick kiln operators often excavate soil deeper than permitted and leave the pits exposed.

“Such pits are much deeper than ordinary ponds and are therefore particularly dangerous for children,” Bhusal said. “Contractors working on roads, bridges and culverts also leave excavations open, either during construction or after the work is completed. Soil is removed during road widening, but the pits are not filled or secured.”

The risk is compounded by poverty.

Police investigations indicate that many children who drown in pits, culverts, brick kiln sites and ponds come from poor or low-income households. Parents who have to work long hours to support their families may be unable to supervise young children closely, leaving them free to wander into ponds, canals and construction sites.

Madhesh Finance Minister Yuvaraj Bhattarai said child safety should be treated as a responsibility shared by families, communities and the state.

“Pits dug in the name of development must no longer take the lives of innocent children,” he said. “The Madhesh government is serious about this.”

On July 5, the secretariat of Janamat Party chair CK Raut said more than 450 children had drowned in ponds and pits in Madhesh over the previous four years. The party argued that the deaths should not be treated simply as natural disasters because many could have been prevented.

It called for open pits in villages and neighbourhoods to be filled or fenced, warning signs and barriers to be installed around ponds, brick kilns and construction sites, and greater supervision of young children around water. It also urged schools and communities to conduct water-safety programmes and local governments to identify and regularly monitor dangerous sites.

The same danger in Lumbini

The problem extends beyond Madhesh.

In the western province of Lumbini, ponds, rivers, irrigation canals and reservoirs are important sources of water, but they also pose a growing drowning risk, particularly during the hot months and monsoon.

In Dang district, an average of about one person dies each month from drowning or being swept away by water, according to Superintendent of Police Dipak Shrestha, chief of District police in Dang. Last fiscal year, 29 people died in such incidents.

Some deaths occur when people who cannot swim enter the water carelessly. Others happen during floods or accidents. Victims have drowned in natural rivers and lakes as well as artificial reservoirs built for irrigation or recreation.

In November 2024, three 12-year-old girls drowned while bathing in the Rapti river.

In June 2024, floodwaters in the Rapti river swept away 62-year-old Maniram Chaudhary of Lamahi Municipality. Seventeen-year-old Raj Kumar Yadav of Rajpur Rural Municipality also drowned while returning home after selling milk. Two teenagers died after being swept away by the Babai river in June.

The broader provincial figures show how widespread the risk is. Lumbini recorded 553 disaster incidents in the past four months, killing 90 people. Sixty of those deaths were caused by drowning, and four people remain missing. Twenty-three of the drowning victims were children.

Last fiscal year, the province recorded 1,837 disasters that killed 297 people. Drowning accounted for 190 deaths, with 14 people still missing.

In Rupandehi district alone, two children and one woman drowned within three months, according to the Butwal Area Police Office. On July 11, 15-year-old Pragya Gautam of Tilottama drowned in a fishpond. She went into the water at about 6pm and was not pulled out until around 9pm.

On May 17, 18-year-old Umakanta Chaudhary of Butwal drowned while swimming in the Tinau River.

Police Inspector Thamman GC said drowning incidents increase during periods of extreme heat, when children and teenagers go swimming in rivers, canals and ponds.

“Children, particularly those aged 11 or 12 and above, often go swimming in groups to escape the heat,” GC said. “They may not know how deep the water is, and that can lead to drowning.”

He said victims were often from low-income or working-class families, or households where parents were away at work.

Last fiscal year, 17 people drowned in Rupandehi, including nine men and eight children. Seven of the children were boys, and one was a girl.

Lumbini authorities have called for stronger safety measures around water infrastructure.

Chief Minister Chet Narayan Acharya, who also chairs the provincial disaster management council, said the government was stepping up awareness campaigns during the monsoon.

“Fencing irrigation canals, ponds and other dangerous water bodies and putting warning signs around public ponds and dams can reduce the risk,” Acharya said. “Local governments have also been instructed to conduct awareness campaigns around canals, ponds, irrigation channels and rivers and to discourage children from swimming in them.”

Prevention remains the missing link

Despite repeated warnings, dangerous sites remain scattered around settlements.

The problem is not limited to natural hazards. In many cases, the danger is created by development itself.

A contractor digs a trench for a culvert and leaves it open. A brick kiln extracts soil and abandons a deep pit. A road project removes earth without restoring the site. A pond or canal is left without a fence or warning sign. Rain then fills the excavation, turning it into a hidden hazard.

“The common factor in Madhesh and Lumbini is the failure to identify water and excavation hazards in places children can reach,” said Dang police chief Shrestha. “In some places, construction pits are left open. In others, there are deep excavations made for brick kilns. Elsewhere, canals, ponds and rivers have no warning signs. Sometimes parental supervision is weak. In other cases, local units and construction companies have failed to do their part.”

Madhav Narayan Municipality Mayor Baijnath Yadav said local units, landowners, industrialists and brick kiln operators all have a role in preventing deaths. Deep excavations should be fenced and marked with warning signs, while old pits that cannot be filled should at least be secured.

Every ward, he said, should map dangerous sites and arrange immediate safety measures. Municipalities should also create safe spaces where children can play instead of turning to construction sites and water-filled pits.

Yadav said his municipality plans to expand public awareness campaigns and provide training on emergency rescue and first aid for drowning victims.

Civil society leader Kedar Thapa of Rautahat said children’s safety must be built into development projects from the beginning.

“Development should improve people’s lives, not become a trap that takes their lives,” he said. “If the authorities do not act in time, more children will continue to disappear into water-filled pits.”

articles.title: Nepal Airlines is making more money, still losing money
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah recently highlighted what he called encouraging signs of recovery at the national flag carrier, Nepal Airlines Corporation.

In a social media post, Shah said the airline had generated Rs6.27 billion in revenue in just four months, achieved an 86 percent occupancy rate and repaid Rs1.06 billion in loan instalments.

But the airline’s own preliminary annual figures paint a not-so-rosy picture.

Nepal Airlines (NAC) estimates that it generated around Rs23.40 billion in revenue in the last fiscal year, while its gross expenses may reach Rs24.40 billion. That would leave the airline with a deficit of about Rs1 billion for the year, despite the increase in revenue.

The corporation has yet to compile its final financial statements. Archana Khadka, the NAC’s corporate director and spokesperson, said income and expenditure figures from several stations were still being compiled. The preliminary figures should therefore not be treated as final, she said, adding that both revenue and expenses could rise once the accounting is completed.

Even so, the preliminary figures indicate that the NAC’s revenue in the fiscal year 2025-26 rose by about 12.5 percent from roughly Rs20.50 billion the previous year. The increase suggests that the airline is getting more business, but its inability to tame expenses continues to undermine its finances.

The NAC had set a far more ambitious target in its budget for the last fiscal year. It projected a total revenue of Rs37.85 billion against an expenditure of Rs37.72 billion, with an expected surplus of about Rs125 million. The preliminary actual revenue is therefore substantially below the budget target.

Ground handling remains a key revenue source

Ground handling remains one of the NAC’s most important sources of income. The airline estimates that it earned around Rs5.71 billion from the service in the last fiscal year, up from about Rs5.04 billion the previous year.

Khadka said the number of international flights had fallen temporarily because of the West Asian conflict, but the impact did not last long. Revenue from ground handling has since increased as more international airlines have begun operating in Nepal, she said.

Around 30 international airlines currently fly to Kathmandu. The NAC provides ground-handling services to most international carriers at the Tribhuvan International Airport, with the exception of Air India.

The corporation had budgeted a Rs7.92 billion ground-handling revenue for the fiscal year. The preliminary actual figure, however, is well below that target.

The latest data shows that while the NAC has managed to expand revenue, it has struggled to keep expenditure under control. The problem is not new. The airline has increased its income in recent years, but repayments on its loans, interest costs, aircraft maintenance and operating expenses have continued to weigh heavily on its balance sheet.

According to the Office of the Auditor General, NAC’s total revenue rose from Rs9.46 billion in the fiscal year 2020-21 to Rs24.21 billion in 2022-23. Despite that growth, the corporation has continued to post losses. It recorded a loss of around Rs1.51 billion in the fiscal year 2023-24, according to the auditor general’s report.

Debt remains NAC’s biggest problem

NAC’s biggest financial burden is its debt.

The corporation borrowed from the Employees Provident Fund and the Citizen Investment Trust to purchase four Airbus aircraft. Repayment of the principal and interest on those loans has become a major strain on the airline’s finances.

According to NAC records, it has so far repaid Rs16.54 billion on the loans taken to purchase the four aircraft. Its preliminary records show that about Rs46.22 billion in liabilities related to those loans remains outstanding. Including other borrowings, NAC’s total debt is estimated at around Rs51 billion.

Khadka said there are some discrepancies between the debt figures maintained by the NAC and those recorded by the lending institutions.

The airline is seeking to reduce its interest burden and restructure its debt, said executive chairman Maheshwor Bhakta Shrestha. NAC is also exploring the possibility of replacing some of its expensive borrowing with loans carrying lower interest rates.

Shrestha said discussions had already been held with the Employees Provident Fund and the Citizen Investment Trust.

The airline borrowed Rs34 billion from the two institutions to purchase the four Airbus planes. It has been paying interest rates of as much as 10.5 percent on those loans. The corporation had projected financial expenses of around Rs4.10 billion for the fiscal year 2025-26 alone.

The corporation believes that reducing its interest burden would narrow the gap between its operating revenue and expenditure and provide some room for financial recovery.

A fleet too small to support expansion

NAC’s operating capacity is also constrained by the condition of its fleet.

The corporation has 11 aircraft, including five Chinese-made planes. Only six are currently operational: two Twin Otters, two narrow-body aircraft and two wide-body aircraft.

Several aircraft have remained grounded for extended periods, limiting the airline’s ability to expand services and make full use of its fleet.

The carrier has repeatedly identified fleet expansion as necessary for increasing both domestic and international services. Its programme for the fiscal year 2025-26 included plans to add narrow-body craft for international routes and study the possibility of leasing aircraft where necessary.

Those plans, however, did not move forward.

Under its budget projections, the NAC planned to operate 2,520 international flights using two Airbus A330s and two A320s and carry more than 865,000 passengers. For domestic services, it had planned 5,174 flights using two Twin Otters.

The airline’s failure to expand its fleet while some existing aircraft remain grounded has limited its ability to increase revenue, even as demand for air travel grows.

The NAC management nevertheless argues that the recent increase in revenue is a positive sign.

Khadka said the income growth should be viewed as an encouraging development. But a sustained financial turnaround will require more than higher revenue, Shrestha said.

The new management is seeking to pursue three objectives simultaneously: increase revenue, control operating costs and reduce the cost of servicing NAC’s debt.

For an airline carrying around Rs51 billion in debt and operating only six of its 11 aircraft, that will be a considerably harder task than the recent rise in revenue figures alone might suggest.

articles.title: Sauraha elephant safari caught between animal welfare and livelihoods
articles.summary:
Sauraha, the country’s major tourist destination in Chitwan, has long been synonymous with elephant safaris. For decades, foreign and domestic tourists visiting Sauraha adjacent to the Chitwan National Park have mounted elephants to traverse the buffer zone’s community forests in search of rare wildlife.

However, the local entrepreneurs who have privately owned and domesticated elephants are worried with a recent Supreme Court verdict. They express their concerns stating that the future of the iconic practice of elephant safaris is in jeopardy. They argue an abrupt halt of elephant safari could devastate the local economy, tourism and harm the animals themselves.

Private elephant owners in Sauraha express readiness to shift toward ethical alternatives, such as elephant-friendly sanctuaries and bushwalks, but contend that a sudden ban is impractical. They are urging authorities to phase out elephants gradually so that owners have time and to adjust their businesses and protect livelihoods.

The delicate issue dominated discussions on Wednesday during the 15th International Elephant Day celebration in Sauraha, where stakeholders gathered for an ‘Elephant Picnic’ organised in the neighbouring Baghmara buffer zone community forest.

“We are prepared to transition to a sanctuary model as envisioned by the court, but it cannot happen overnight,” said Dipendra Khatiwada, the president of the United Elephant Management Cooperative Limited. “We are not in favour of stopping elephant safaris at once. We should instead pursue a dual-track approach: allow fit, working-age elephants to continue safaris for a few more years, while creating dedicated sanctuaries for elderly, sick, or disabled elephants and integrating them into tourism activities that do not disturb nature and local communities.”

The high-profile legal dispute stems from a writ petition filed on September 14, 2021, by advocate Sanjay Adhikari and others on behalf of the Janahit Samrakshan Manch. The petitioners demanded an end to animal cruelty, better record-keeping to curb illegal trading, a prohibition on chaining, and a complete phase-out of elephant rides in favour of observation-only tourism.

On December 17 last year, the Supreme Court ruled in favour of animal welfare reforms. The full text verdict was recently uploaded to the Supreme Court’s website, laying out comprehensive guidelines for elephant conservation and directing the government to seek alternatives to riding safaris.

“The anatomical structure of an elephant’s spine, legs, and body is not evolved to carry human passengers,” the court noted in point 48 of the verdict. “Subjecting these animals to heavy loads and continuous circular tours causes severe physical stress, foot rot, and joint ailments. Using an elephant merely as a tool for human entertainment contradicts our legal duty to respect its intrinsic worth and welfare as a living biological entity.”

In point 51, the justices instructed the government to establish clear legal policies transitioning Nepal towards ethical eco-tourism, drawing upon international precedents such as “elephant bushwalks” and observation platforms that maintain a safe distance between visitors and animals.

In the verdict, the Supreme Court has directed the government and agencies concerned to make the registration and management of privately owned and domesticated elephants more systematic. Under Rule 12 of the Regulation on the Control of International Trade of Endangered Wildlife and Plants, 2019, all such elephants must be registered and properly documented. Authorities must identify unregistered elephants and take action under existing laws. Any transfer of ownership, sale, purchase or movement of elephants must also be subject to legal approval and proper record-keeping.

The court has also called for stronger measures to control the illegal trade and cross-border smuggling of elephants. Security agencies, forest authorities and conservation bodies should coordinate effectively, particularly along the Nepal-India border, and maintain special surveillance. Individuals or organisations involved in the illegal sale, transportation or smuggling of elephants should be investigated and prosecuted in accordance with the law.

On elephant welfare, the court has ordered authorities to prevent torture, violence and other forms of inhumane treatment. It has called for scientific and animal-friendly methods of elephant management and urged that tourism involving elephants be made more welfare-friendly.

Mahouts and caretakers should receive training in elephant-friendly practices, while proper treatment and protection should be ensured for sick and ageing elephants. The court has also called for the establishment of elephant retirement and rehabilitation centres.

The court has directed authorities to move towards a chain-free and more natural system of keeping privately owned elephants. Elephants should be provided with open and natural surroundings, while management plans should take into account possible conflicts between people and elephants, as well as between wild and domesticated elephants. Drawing on international practices in elephant welfare and conservation, Nepal should gradually develop and implement scientific standards for elephant management.

The court has further called for ethical elephant sanctuaries where tourists can observe elephants only from a safe distance rather than ride or directly interact with them. The practice of keeping elephants unnecessarily chained, whether for training or other purposes, should be ended. Authorities have been asked to develop and implement policies and action plans to make elephant conservation centres and management systems more scientific and welfare-oriented.

The verdict also calls for better coordination among all agencies involved in elephant conservation and management. Regular monitoring of conservation activities should be carried out, and clear standards for the management of privately owned elephants should be developed and enforced.

The local operators argue that forcing an immediate shutdown without a transitional safety net would lead to financial ruin and widespread job displacement.

A single adult elephant commands a market price between Rs10 million and Rs15 million, while monthly maintenance, feed, and healthcare costs range from Rs100,000 to Rs120,000. Each animal requires at least two full-time handlers: a phaneta to manage feeding and grooming, and a mahout to handle movement and general care.

“If owners are forbidden from offering safaris, who will pay to feed and care for these massive animals?” asked Dipendra, who previously owned two elephants but now retains only one, Chanchalkali. “Following the Covid pandemic, when tourism collapsed, many owners were forced to sell their animals to buyers in India. In Sauraha, private elephant numbers dropped from 90 to around 45 today. A sudden ban without financial support will lead to complete abandonment.”

The looming ban has cast a shadow over the lives of local handlers. Jayalal Das, 48, a mahout from Rautahat who cares for an elephant named Sherkali, relies entirely on his income to support his six-member family. His grandfather was a mahout, and Das has spent 18 years in Sauraha driving tourist safaris.

“I do not know any other skilled work,” said Das. “If safaris close down tomorrow, I will have no way to feed my four children.” Nandalal Sah, who handles another private elephant named Ektakali, shared similar worries, adding softly, “If there are no elephants left to ride, I will have no choice but to do manual labour.”

Unlike government-owned elephants, which are strictly reserved for national park patrolling, research, and anti-poaching operations, all commercial safari elephants in Sauraha are privately owned and operate strictly within buffer zone community forests rather than the core protected park.

Addressing the gathering, Chief Conservation Officer of Chitwan National Park Dil Bahadur Purja Pun, acknowledged the binding legal reality of the ruling. He advised stakeholders to collaborate with park authorities to implement humanely managed elephant welfare practices while gradually aligning local tourism operations with the directives set by the Supreme Court.

articles.title: नेपाली लोक-रक ब्यान्ड नेपथ्यकाे गान्तोकमा सांगीतिक प्रस्तुति
articles.summary:
नेपाली लोक–रक ब्यान्ड नेपथ्यले पहिलोपटक भारतको सिक्किमस्थित गान्तोकमा सांगीतिक प्रस्तुति दिने भएको छ। आगामी ३१ अक्टोबर २०२६ मा गान्तोकको पाल्जोर स्टेडियममा ‘नेपथ्य लाइभ इन सिक्किम–लेट्स गेट लाउडः सेलिब्रेट सिक्किम’मा नेपथ्यले आफूलाई प्रस्तुत गर्न लगेको हो।

पोजिटिभ भाइब्स इन्टरटेनमेन्ट नेटवर्क (पीभीई नेटवर्क) को प्रस्तुतिमा र नेपालयको निर्माणमा हुन लागेको कन्सर्टलाई संगीत, संस्कृति र पर्यटनलाई जोड्ने उत्सवका रूपमा आयोजना गर्न लागिएको आयोजकले जनाएको छ।

‘रेशम’, ‘तालको पानी’, ‘भेडाको ऊन जस्तो’, ‘जोमसोमै बजारमा’ र ‘यो जिन्दगानी’ लगायतका गीतमार्फत विभिन्न पुस्ताका नेपालीभाषी श्रोतामाझ लोकप्रिय नेपथ्यको यो गान्तोकमा पहिलो प्रस्तुति हुनेछ।

कार्यक्रममा सिक्किमसँगै भारतको उत्तरपूर्वी क्षेत्र, भारतका विभिन्न भाग, भुटान र नेपालबाट समेत दर्शक सहभागी हुने आयोजकको भनाई छ। दसैं–तिहारको चाडपर्वको बीचमा आयोजना हुने भएकाले कार्यक्रमले साथीभाइ, परिवार र संगीतप्रेमीलाई कन्सर्टसँगै गान्तोक र सिक्किमको संस्कृति, प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्य तथा पर्यटन अनुभव गर्ने अवसर प्रदान गर्ने आयोजकको दाबी छ।

पीभीई नेटवर्कका संस्थापक निर्देशक बिकेश कायस्थले ‘लेट्स गेट लाउडः सेलिब्रेट सिक्किम’को उद्देश्य सांगीतिक कार्यक्रम मात्र नभई संगीतलाई माध्यम बनाएर सिक्किमका मानिस, संस्कृति, सम्पदा, प्राकृतिक सौन्दर्य र आतिथ्यलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्दै राज्यलाई सांस्कृतिक तथा सांगीतिक पर्यटन गन्तव्यका रूपमा स्थापित गर्ने हो।

‘यो कन्सर्ट मात्र होइन, संगीतमार्फत सिक्किमलाई उत्सवका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्ने हाम्रो प्रयास हो,’ कायस्थले भने, ‘नेपाल, भुटान, भारतको उत्तरपूर्वी क्षेत्र र भारतका विभिन्न भागबाट दर्शक गान्तोक आऊन्, नेपथ्यको संगीतसँगै सिक्किमको संस्कृति, मानिस र पर्यटनलाई अनुभव गरून् भन्ने हाम्रो चाहना हो।’

उनका अनुसार ‘सेलिब्रेट सिक्किम’मार्फत सिक्किमलाई सांस्कृतिक तथा सांगीतिक पर्यटन गन्तव्यका रूपमा अघि बढाउने दीर्घकालीन सोचसमेत राखिएको छ।

पीभीई नेटवर्कले सन् २०२५ मा सज्जनराज वैद्यको प्रस्तुतिसहित ‘लेट्स गेट लाउड सिक्किम’ आयोजना गरेको थियो। आयोजकका अनुसार उक्त कार्यक्रममा पाँच हजारभन्दा बढी दर्शक सहभागी भएका थिए। तीमध्ये दुई हजारभन्दा बढी सिक्किम बाहिरबाट कार्यक्रमका लागि आएका थिए।

बाहिरबाट आएका दर्शकको आवास, होटल तथा रेस्टुरेन्ट, यातायात, स्थानीय किनमेल, सेवा तथा अन्य खर्चका कारण उक्त कार्यक्रमले सिक्किमको स्थानीय बजारमा तीन करोड भारतीय रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको आर्थिक गतिविधि सिर्जना गरेको पीभीई नेटवर्कले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: एकैदिन ४६ सयले घट्यो सुन, चाँदी पनि सस्तियो
articles.summary:
नेपाली सुनचाँदी बजारमा शुक्रबार सुन र चाँदी दुवैको मूल्य घटेको छ।

आज सुन एकैदिन प्रतितोला चार हजार ६ सय रूपैयाँ घटेको नेपाल सुनचाँदी व्यवसायी महासंघले जनाएको छ।

यससँगै आज सुन प्रतितोला तीन लाख एक हजार ६ सय रूपैयाँमा कारोबार भइरहेको छ। बिहीबार सुन प्रतितोला तीन लाख ६ हजार दुई सय रूपैयाँमा कारोबार भएको थियो।

यस्तै, शुक्रबार चाँदीको मूल्य पनि घटेको छ। आज चाँदी प्रतितोला ९० रूपैयाँले घटेर चार हजार ६ सय ६० रूपैयाँमा कारोबार भइरहेको महासंघले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: रोल्पा : उद्धारका लागि गएको टोली पहिरोमा फसेपछि...
articles.summary:
बुधबार राति रोल्पाको थबाङ गाउँपालिका–५ कोटलबारामा पहिरो गएको खबर पाए संगै बिहीबार बिहान ४ बजे उद्धार टोली लिएर घटनास्थल पुगेको सुरक्षाकर्मीको टोली सदरमुकाम फर्कँदा आफैँ अर्को पहिरोमा फसेको छ।

सुनछहरी गाउँपालिका १ जैमाजा सिरक्याङ भिरको नजिकै रहेको सोनारे बस्तीमा पुगेका उनीहरू सदरमुकाम फर्किने सडकमा पहिरो खसेका कारण अलपत्र परेका हुन्।

१० जनाको मृत्यु, ३ जना बेपत्ता, २ जना घाइते भएको उक्त घटना उद्धार गरेर फर्कने क्रममा रोल्पाका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी गंगाबहादुर क्षेत्री, लुम्बिनी प्रदेशका प्रहरी प्रमुख डिआईजी भुपेन्द्रबहादुर खत्री, नेपाली सेनाका कर्णेल दिपेश खड्का, रोल्पा प्रहरी प्रमुख पंचकुमार बाखु, सशस्त्र डिएसपी कालिप्रसाद चौधरीसहितको उद्धार टोली रातभर सडकमै अलपत्र परेको हो।

सुरक्षाकर्मीको टोली संगै लुम्बिनी प्रदेशका निवर्तमान मुख्यमन्त्री जोखबहादुर महरा, सुनछहरी गाउँपालिका अध्यक्ष धनबहादुर पुन, थबाङ गाउँपालिका अध्यक्ष सबिन बुढा मगर, सुनिल स्मृति गाउँपालिका अध्यक्ष मनिराम बुढाथोकी, नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीको टिमलगायत करिब १ सय जना उद्धार टोली रातभर गाडीमा बसेको थियो।

‘दिनभरको भोक। सबै थाकेका। यहाँ आउँदा पहिरो गएको स्थान नेर एउटा मात्र घर थियो,’ सुनछहरी गाउँपालिकाका अध्यक्ष धनबहादुर पुनले नागरिकसँग कुरा गर्दै भने, ‘उक्त घरमा ४ पाथि गहुँ रैछ त्यही किनेर भुट्यौँ अनि करिब १ सय जनाले एक-एक मुठि बाँडेर खायौँ। पहिरोको त्रासमा रातभर गाडीमा बसेर उज्यालो बनायौँ।’

छिमेकी पालिका थबाङको कोटलबारामा पहिरो पीडितको उद्धारका लागि गएका धनबहादुर यति बेला अर्को समस्यामा परेका छन्। बिहीबार रातिको अविरल बर्षातपछि आएको पहिरोले आफ्नो गाउँपालिकाको गाममा गएको पहिरोले ४ जनाको पुरेको खबर पाएसंगै आत्तिएका छन्। ‘गाममा पहिरोले ४ जना पुरेको खबर आछ तर १२ नबज्दै यो पहिरो खुल्दैन। त्यहाँ पुग्न गाडीमा ४/५ घण्टा हिँडेर अरू पैदल ३ घण्टा जति लाग्छ।’

प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी गंगाबहादुर क्षेत्रीले आफूहरू पैदल अगाडि बढेको बताए। ‘गाडी उतै छोडेर पैदल हिँडेका छौँ। ५ घण्टा भो हिँडेको,’ क्षेत्रीले भने, ‘गाममा फेरि पहिरोले ४ जना पुरिएको खबर आएको छ। त्यहाँ उद्धारका लागि सुरक्षाको अर्को टोली मुभ भएको छ।’

उनका अनुसार पूर्वी रोल्पाका धेरै गाउँ यति बेला पहिरोको जोखिममा छन्।

articles.title: श्रेष्ठलाई सोमबार उपस्थित गराउन सर्वोच्चको आदेश
articles.summary:
सर्वोच्च अदालतले पत्रकार किशोर श्रेष्ठलाई बरामद सामग्रीसहित सोमबार अदालतमा उपस्थित गराउन आदेश दिएको छ। बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरणको रिटमाथि सुनुवाइपछि न्यायाधीश बालकृष्ण ढकालको एकल इजलासले श्रेष्ठलाई उपस्थित गराउन आदेश दिएको हो।

श्रेष्ठकी श्रीमती सरस्वतीले उनको गैरकानुनी थुनाविरुद्ध बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरणको रिट दायर गरेकी थिइन्। बुधबार राति पक्राउ परेका श्रेष्ठलाई हाल जिल्ला प्रहरी परिसर, भद्रकालीबाट महाराजगञ्जस्थित प्रहरी वृत्तको हिरासतमा सारिएको छ।

जिल्ला प्रहरी परिसरमा थुनुवाको चाप रहेकाले मुद्दाको अनुसन्धान तथा अभियोजनमा सहजताका लागि उनलाई बिहीबार साँझ महाराजगञ्जस्थित प्रहरी वृत्तमा सारिएको जिल्ला प्रहरी परिषद्ले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: Supreme Court orders authorities to present Kishor Shrestha in court
articles.summary:
The Supreme Court has ordered authorities to explain why journalist Kishor Shrestha should not be released, two days after police arrested the editor of the weekly Jana Aastha.

A single bench of Justice Bal Krishna Dhakal issued the show-cause order on Friday in response to a habeas corpus petition filed on Shrestha’s behalf by his wife, Saraswati Shrestha.

The court ordered the authorities to submit a written response by Monday, along with Shrestha in person. It also directed them to bring the investigation file, including the complaint filed against him, as well as electronic devices seized from his home and office, including a CPU, laptop, iPad and mobile phone.

The Kathmandu District Court on Thursday authorised police to detain Shrestha for three days for investigation. Police arrested him late Wednesday from Lalitpur, saying he was being investigated for allegedly violating Nepal’s Privacy Act, 2018.

The arrest has sparked a widespread debate, with opinions sharply divided.

While a large section of the media fraternity has criticised the arrest, calling the move an attack on the free press, others have welcomed it, levelling allegations against him that, under the guise of journalism, he was perpetrating violence against women.

The Federation of Nepali Journalists, the country’s largest journalists’ organisation, staged a protest outside the Kathmandu District Police Range on Thursday and demanded Shrestha’s unconditional release.

In a statement, FNJ general secretary Ram Prasad Dahal accused the authorities of engaging in “anti-press” conduct and said disputes over news content should be handled through the Press Council Nepal rather than criminal investigations.

The FNJ said the police action amounted to an encroachment on the Press Council’s jurisdiction.

“The Press Council Nepal has jurisdiction over complaints concerning news content,” the federation said, arguing that using state machinery to investigate a journalist’s source was contrary to press freedom, freedom of expression and the constitution.

Police raided the Jana Aastha weekly office in Jhamsikhel, Lalitpur, early Thursday, hours after Shrestha’s arrest. Investigators seized computers and other electronic equipment as part of the inquiry, according to Kathmandu District Police Range spokesperson Superintendent of Police Dan Bahadur Thapa.

articles.title: नेपाली कांग्रेस सरकार असफल होस् भन्ने चाहना राख्दैन
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेसका उपसभापति विश्वप्रकाश शर्माले वर्तमान सरकार असफल होस् भन्ने कांग्रेसको चाहना नरहेको बताएका छन् ।

शुक्रबार बसेको कांग्रेस केन्द्रीय कार्यसमितिको बैठकअघि बोल्दै शर्माले प्रतिपक्षमा रहेको दलले सामान्यतया सरकार असफल भएको हेर्न चाहने भए पनि कांग्रेसले त्यस्तो धारणा नराखेको बताए ।

उनले नयाँ सरकारको नीति तथा कार्यक्रम असफल हुँदा त्यसले समाजमा निराशा ल्याउने भएकाले कांग्रेसले प्रतिनिधिसभामा अवरोध गरे पनि राष्ट्रिय सभाबाट सरकारको नीति तथा कार्यक्रम पारित गर्न सहयोग गरेको स्मरण गरे ।

शर्माले भने, ‘सरकारको असफलता हामी चाहँदैनौँ। सामान्यतया प्रतिपक्षीको स्वरबाट सुनिँदै गर्दा सरकारको असफलताको अपेक्षा हुन्छ। तर यही कांग्रेस पार्टीले प्रतिनिधिसभामा उभिएर प्रधानमन्त्रीको खोजी गर्दै सरकारको नीति तथा कार्यक्रम पारित गर्ने बेला अवरोध गरिरहेको अवस्थामा त्यही दिन राष्ट्रिय सभामा उभिएर कांग्रेस पार्टीले सरकारको नीति तथा कार्यक्रम पारित गर्न सघाएको थियो।’

शर्माले कांग्रेस विगतभन्दा पृथक ढंगले अघि बढिरहेको दाबी गर्दै पार्टीका नेता तथा कार्यकर्ताले त्यसलाई आत्मसात गर्नुपर्ने बताए । उनले कांग्रसको देउवा पक्षलाई संकेत गर्दै पार्टी केन्द्रले अघि सारेको नयाँ अभियानसँग सबै एक ठाउँमा उभिएर अघि बढ्नुपर्ने बताए ।

उनले भने, ‘कांग्रेस विगतमा भन्दा पृथक ढंगले काम गरिरहेको छ । यो यथार्थलाई आज सुरु भएको राष्ट्रिय भेलाका प्रत्येक साथीहरूले पनि मनन गर्न जरुरी छ ।’

निवर्तमान सभापति शेरबहादुर देउवा काठमाडौं फर्किएपछि कांग्रेसले स्वागत गरेको स्मरण गर्दै शर्माले देउवाबाट पार्टीका सबै नेता–कार्यकर्ताको कुरा सुन्ने प्रतिबद्धताको अपेक्षा गरिएको बताए ।

उनले देउवाले लिखित अभिव्यक्तिमार्फत परिवर्तनलाई आत्मसात गर्ने र युवालाई अगाडि बढाउने विषय उल्लेख गरेको भन्दै आगामी सम्मेलनमा पनि त्यसलाई केन्द्रमा राख्नुपर्ने बताए ।

‘हाम्रो अपेक्षा थियो निर्वतमान सभापतिले बोल्दैगर्दा भनिदिनपर्ने थियो म लामो समयपछि देश फर्केको छु, सबैको सुन्न चाहान्छु । यद्यपी, लिखित अभिव्यक्ति आएको छ । परिवर्तनलाई आत्मसाथ गर्न चाहन्छु र युवा अगाडि बढाउने कुरा गर्नुभएको छ । राष्ट्रिय सम्मेलनले पनि त्यो कुरालाई केन्द्रमा राखोस,’ उनले भने ।

शर्माले नेपाली कांग्रेस विधि, पद्धति र प्रक्रियामार्फत परिवर्तनको अध्यायमा प्रवेश गरिसकेको दाबी गरे ।

articles.title: जेनजी आन्दोलनका घाइते र सहिद परिवारसँग सम्झौता कार्यान्वयन गर्न सहजीकरण समिति गठन
articles.summary:
सरकारले गत वर्ष भदौ २३/२४ मा भएको जेन–जी आन्दोलनका क्रममा भएका घाइते तथा सहिद परिवारका सम्झौता कार्यान्वयनका लागि सहजीकरण समिति गठन गरेको छ।

शुक्रबार आयोजित प्रेस ब्रिफिङमा प्रधानमन्त्री तथा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को कार्यालयका सहसचिव हेमराज अर्यालले उक्त जानकारी दिएका हुन्।

प्रधानमन्त्री तथा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को कार्यालयका सहसचिवको संयोजकत्वमा गठित ‘जेनजी सम्झौता तथा एकीकृत प्याकेज कार्यान्वयन समन्वय एवं सहजीकरण समिति’ ले सरकार र आन्दोलनकारी पक्षबीच भएका सम्झौताहरूको कार्यान्वयन र समन्वयमा मुख्य भूमिका खेल्नेछ जनाइएको छ।

नेपाल सरकार र जेन–जी प्रतिनिधिहरूबीच २०८२ मङ्सिर २४ गते भएको सम्झौता र मन्त्रिपरिषद्को २०८३ असार १८ गतेको बैठकबाट स्वीकृत भएको ‘एकीकृत प्याकेज’ को कार्यान्वयनको प्रगति समीक्षा गर्ने मुख्य जिम्मेवारी यस समितिलाई तोकिएको छ।

समितिले प्याकेज कार्यान्वयनका लागि विभिन्न मन्त्रालयहरूबीच आपसी समन्वय पनि कायम गराउनेछ। यो समितिले आन्दोलनका घाइते तथा सहिद परिवारका लागि प्रत्यक्ष सम्पर्क विन्दुको रूपमा काम गर्नेछ।

मन्त्रिपरिषद्‍बाट स्वीकृत प्याकेजमा व्यवस्था भएबमोजिम प्रभावित परिवारहरूको शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा रोजगारीसमेतका संवेदनशील विषयहरू कार्यान्वयनमा ल्याउन समितिले विभिन्न सरकारी निकायहरूसँग आवश्यक समन्वय र सहजीकरण गर्ने कार्यादेश पाएको छ।

सम्झौता र प्याकेज कार्यान्वयनका क्रममा आउन सक्ने व्यावहारिक समस्या वा जटिलताहरू समाधान गर्न समितिले आवश्यक सुधारका उपायहरू पहिल्याई सम्बन्धित निकायहरूमा सिफारिस गर्नेछ।

आफ्नो कार्यादेश बमोजिम काम गर्ने क्रममा समितिले आवश्यकताअनुसार सरकारी वा गैर–सरकारी प्रतिनिधि तथा विषयगत विशेषज्ञ (विज्ञ) व्यक्तिहरूलाई समेत आमन्त्रण गरी छलफल र बैठकहरू सञ्चालन गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ।

सहसचिव अर्यालको संयोजकत्वमा गठित यस समितिको सदस्यहरूमा गृह मन्त्रालय, अर्थ मन्त्रालय, शिक्षा तथा खेलकुद मन्त्रालय, युवा, श्रम तथा रोजगार मन्त्रालय, पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्रालय, स्वास्थ्य तथा खाद्य स्वच्छता मन्त्रालय र महिला, बालबालिका, लैङ्गिक तथा यौनिक अल्पसङ्ख्यक र सामाजिक सुरक्षा मन्त्रालयबाट एकरएक जना उपसचिव तथा जेनजी आन्दोलनका सहिद परिवार र घाइते परिवारका तर्फबाट दुई/दुई जना छन्।

समितिको सदस्य सचिवमा प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयका उपसचिव वासुदेव खनाल छन्।

articles.title: शशांक कोइरालाले भनेः वीपीले शेरबहादुरलाई पश्चिमको राजकुमार भन्नुहुन्थ्यो
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेसका नेता डा.शशांक कोइरालाले पार्टीलाई एकजुट बनाउन राष्ट्रिय भेला आयोजना गरेको बताएका छन्।

काठमाडौंमा शुक्रबार उद्घाटन सत्रलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै राष्ट्रिय भेलाका संयोजक डा.कोइरालाले शेरबहादुर देउवाको उपस्थितिले भेला पूर्णरुपमा सफल भइसकेको दाबी गरे। उनले भने, 'नेपाली कांग्रेसलाई एक बनाउन भेला आयोजना गरेको हो। पार्टी एकजुट भएको खण्डमा कसैले पराजित गर्न नसक्ने कुरा यथार्थ हो।'

डा.कोइरालाले आफ्ना बुवा वीपी कोइरालाले शेरबहादुर देउवालाई पश्चिमको राजकुमार भन्ने गरेको चर्चा पनि गरे। भारतमा बसेका समय देउवासँग चलचित्र हेर्न गएको प्रशंग उठाउँदै डा.कोइरालाले वीपीले देउवाको क्षमता त्यही समयदेखि जानेको बताएका थिए।

उद्घाटन सत्रमा कांग्रेसइतर पक्षले देउवालाई पार्टी सभापतिका रुपमा आशनग्रहण गराएको छ भने वक्ताहरुले सभापतिका रुपमा सम्बोधन गरिरहेका छन्।

articles.title: दल दर्ता गरेपछि धवलशम्शेरले दुर्गा प्रसाईंलाई दिए सहकार्यको निम्तो
articles.summary:
डा.धवलशम्शेर राणाले नयाँ राजनीतिक दल ‘जय नेपाल पार्टी’ दर्ता गराएका छन् । शुक्रबार राणाले नयाँ पार्टी दर्ताका लागि निर्वाचन आयोग पुगेका थिए ।

दल दर्तापछि सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै राणाले दुर्गा प्रसाईंलाई पार्टीमा सहभागी हुन स्वागत गर्ने बताए । उनले प्रसाईं र आफूहरूबीच पछि सहकार्य हुने जानकारी दिए ।

‘हामी दुर्गा प्रसाईंको प्रतीक्षामै छौँ । उहाँ आउनुहुन्छ भने स्वागत नै छ । अहिले जय नेपाल पार्टी दर्ता भएको छ । दुर्गा प्रसाईंजी हुनुहुन्न । उहाँले हामी पछि मिल्छौँ भन्नुभएको छ,’ राणाले भने ।

राणाका अनुसार जय नेपाल पार्टीले चुनाव चिह्नका रूपमा ‘त्रिभुज’ पाएको छ । त्रिभुजलाई हिमाल, पहाड र तराई तथा सनातन धर्म, राजसंस्था र प्रजातन्त्रका रूपमा व्याख्या गरिएको उनले बताए । पार्टीको झण्डा सेतो रंगको हुने र त्यसमा रातो त्रिभुज रहने उनले जानकारी दिए ।

राणाले आगामी स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनलाई लक्षित गर्दै पार्टी दर्ता गरिएको बताए । उनका अनुसार जय नेपाल पार्टीले देशभरका सबै स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनमा सहभागी हुने तयारी गरेको छ ।

‘स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनका लागि नै हामीले तयारी गर्न दल दर्ता गरेका हौँ । सम्पूर्ण स्थानीय तहको निर्वाचनमा हामी सहभागी हुन्छौँ,’ उनले भने ।

उनले स्थानीय तहमा सेवा गर्न इच्छुक र इमानदारीपूर्वक काम गर्न चाहने नेपाली नागरिकलाई जय नेपाल पार्टीबाट निर्वाचनमा सहभागी हुन आवेदन दिन आह्वानसमेत गरे ।
